questions.text: What is the purpose of web form? Write a program to demonstrate the concept of collection and generics.
questions.html: What is the purpose of web form? Write a program to demonstrate the concept of collection and generics.
questions.answerHtml:
The purpose of a web form is to enable users to submit data to a web server for processing. It allows users to enter information, make selections, and perform actions on a web page. The data submitted through a web form can be processed on the server-side to perform various operations, such as storing data in a database, sending emails, performing calculations, or generating dynamic content.

Here’s an example program that demonstrates the concept of collections and generics in C#:

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
class Program
{
static void Main()
{
// Create a list of strings
List<string> names = new List<string>();
// Add elements to the list
names.Add(“Ankit”);
names.Add(“Kushal”);
names.Add(“Suraj”);
// Display the elements
Console.WriteLine(“Names:”);
foreach (string name in names)
{
Console.WriteLine(name);
}
// Create a dictionary of string keys and int values
Dictionary<string, int> ages = new Dictionary<string, int>();
// Add key-value pairs to the dictionary
ages.Add(“Ankit”, 25);
ages.Add(“Kushal”, 30);
ages.Add(“Suraj”, 35);
// Display the elements
Console.WriteLine(“\nAges:”);
foreach (KeyValuePair<string, int> pair in ages)
{
Console.WriteLine(pair.Key + “: ” + pair.Value);
}
}
}

When you run this code, the output will be:

Names:
Ankit
Kushal
Suraj
Ages:
Ankit: 25
Kushal: 30
Suraj: 35

In this example, we create a list of strings called `names` using the `List<string>` type. We add elements to the list using the `Add` method and then iterate over the collection to display the names. Next, we create a dictionary called `ages` using the `Dictionary<string, int>` type, where the keys are strings representing names and the values are integers representing ages. We use the `Add` method to add key-value pairs to the dictionary, and then iterate over the collection to display the names and ages.

questions.text: Explain the uses of cookies. What types of vulnerabilities can occur in web application? Show the case of Cross-site Scripting attack.
questions.html: Explain the uses of cookies. What types of vulnerabilities can occur in web application? Show the case of Cross-site Scripting attack.
questions.answerHtml:
Cookies are small pieces of data that are stored on a user’s device by a website. They are sent by the web server to the browser and are stored locally on the user’s device. Cookies are commonly used to manage user sessions. When a user logs into a website, a session cookie is created, which allows the server to identify the user across different requests. This helps maintain the user’s authentication state and enables personalized experiences. Cookies can also be used for security purposes, such as storing session tokens or authentication-related information. By using secure and encrypted cookies, websites can enhance the security of user sessions and protect against unauthorized access. Vulnerabilities in .NET Core applications refer to weaknesses or flaws in the code, configuration, or architecture of applications developed using the .NET Core framework. These vulnerabilities can potentially be exploited by attackers to compromise the security or functionality of the application, leading to unauthorized access, data breaches, or other malicious activities. Cross site scripting attack, Sql injection attack, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) & Open Redirect Attacks are one of the most common vulnerabilities.

Cross-site Scripting (XSS) is a security vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users. Here’s a example of a non-persistent (or reflected) Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack in ASP.NET Core:

Consider the following vulnerable ASP.NET Core Razor Page:

Search.cshtml

@page
@model SearchModel
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<title>Search Page</title>
</head>
<body>
<form method=”get”>
<input type=”text” name=”query” placeholder=”Search…”>
<input type=”submit” value=”Search”>
</form>
<h3>Search Results:</h3>
<p>Your search results for ‘@Model.Query’:</p>
</body>
</html>

Search.cshtml.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages;
namespace XSSExample.Pages
{
public class SearchModel : PageModel
{
public string Query { get; set; }
public void OnGet(string query)
{
Query = query;
}
}
}

In this example, a user can submit a search query through the form, and the value is displayed within a paragraph (`<p>`) tag without any encoding or sanitization. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious script within the search query. For instance, they can use the following query:

<script>alert(‘XSS Attack!’);</script>

If the user enters this query, the script will be executed when the search results page loads for other users, potentially leading to malicious actions. To prevent XSS attacks in ASP.NET Core, you should always perform proper input validation, encoding, and output escaping.

questions.text: Describe any two hosting models for core application. Design a client side validation application using jquery for taking input data from student in Library Management System, assume your own assumptions.
questions.html: Describe any two hosting models for core application. Design a client side validation application using jquery for taking input data from student in Library Management System, assume your own assumptions.
questions.answerHtml:
Two hosting models for ASP.NET Core applications are:

Self-Hosting Model:

In the self-hosting model, the ASP.NET Core application is responsible for hosting itself using a lightweight web server. It does not rely on a separate web server like IIS. Instead, it uses the Kestrel web server, which is a cross-platform, open-source web server built into ASP.NET Core. This model allows the application to be self-contained and deployed as a standalone executable, making it suitable for scenarios where full IIS hosting is not required or available.

IIS Hosting Model: In the IIS hosting model, the ASP.NET Core application is hosted within Internet Information Services (IIS). It leverages the IIS web server to handle HTTP requests and manage the application’s lifecycle. The application runs as a module within the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe). This model provides benefits such as process isolation, enhanced scalability, and the ability to take
advantage of IIS features and configurations, such as load balancing, SSL termination, and URL rewriting.

Here’s an example of a client-side validation application using jQuery for a Library Management System student registration form

StudentRegistration.cshtml

@page
@model StudentRegistrationModel
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<title>Library Management System – Student Registration</title>
<script src=”https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.6.0.min.js”></script>
<script>
$(document).ready(function() {
$(“#registrationForm”).submit(function(e) {
e.preventDefault(); // Prevent form submission
// Perform client-side validation
var name = $(“#name”).val();
var rollNumber = $(“#rollNumber”).val();
if (name === “”) {
alert(“Please enter your name”);
return;
}
if (rollNumber === “”) {
alert(“Please enter your roll number”);
return;
}
// If all validations pass, submit the form to the server
$(“#registrationForm”).unbind(“submit”).submit();
});
});
</script>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Student Registration</h1>
<form id=”registrationForm” method=”post”>
<label for=”name”>Name:</label>
<input type=”text” id=”name” name=”Name” />
<label for=”rollNumber”>Roll Number:</label>
<input type=”text” id=”rollNumber” name=”RollNumber” />
<input type=”submit” value=”Register” />
</form>
</body>
</html>

StudentRegistration.cshtml.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages;
namespace LibraryManagement.Pages
{
public class StudentRegistrationModel : PageModel
{
public void OnGet()
{
}
}
}

In this example, we have an ASP.NET Core Razor Page for student registration. The form includes name and roll number fields. The jQuery code performs client-side validation when the form is submitted. It checks if the name and roll number fields are filled in. If any of the validations fail, an alert message is
displayed. If all validations pass, the form is submitted to the server.

questions.text: How to you assign roles, claims and policies? Explain with an example.
questions.html: How to you assign roles, claims and policies? Explain with an example.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Roles:

Roles represent groups or categories of users with specific privileges or permissions. Suppose you have a simple web application with two roles: Admin and User. You can assign roles to users during registration or in the user management section.

[Authorize(Roles = “Admin”)]
public IActionResult AdminDashboard()
{
// Code for the admin dashboard
}

In this example, the `AdminDashboard` action is only accessible to users in the “Admin” role. Users in the “User” role would be denied access to this action.

2. Claims:

Claims are pieces of information about a user, such as their username, email, or any custom information. Let’s consider a scenario where you have an application with a claim called “Age” that represents the age of a user. You can assign this claim to a user during authentication or based on their data.

services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
options.AddPolicy(“AdultOnly”, policy =>
policy.RequireClaim(“Age”, “18”, “19”, “20”));
});

In this example, the “AdultOnly” policy requires the user to have an “Age” claim of “18”, “19”, or “20” to access the associated resources or actions.

3. Policies:

Policies are a flexible way to define authorization rules based on various conditions, such as roles, claims, or custom requirements. Suppose you have a policy that allows access to certain actions only during business hours.

public class BusinessHoursRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement
{
// Custom requirement logic
}
public class BusinessHoursHandler : AuthorizationHandler<BusinessHoursRequirement>
{
protected override Task HandleRequirementAsync(AuthorizationHandlerContext context, BusinessHoursRequirementrequirement)
{
// Check if it’s business hours and succeed or fail the requirement
}
}

services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
options.AddPolicy(“BusinessHoursPolicy”, policy =>
policy.Requirements.Add(new BusinessHoursRequirement()));
});

In this example, the “BusinessHoursPolicy” requires the custom requirement “BusinessHoursRequirement” to be satisfied. The custom handler “BusinessHoursHandler” determines whether the requirement is met based on the current time.

questions.text: What types of problems lead to SQL injection attack? Discuss any two types of ASP.Net host models.
questions.html: What types of problems lead to SQL injection attack? Discuss any two types of ASP.Net host models.
questions.answerHtml:
SQL injection attacks occur due to vulnerabilities in the way an application handles user input and constructs SQL queries. The following problems can lead to SQL injection attacks:

– If an application fails to validate and sanitize user input before using it in SQL queries, it becomes vulnerable to SQL injection attacks.
– If the application does not properly sanitize or escape special characters in the input, an attacker can manipulate the query structure by injecting SQL code.
– If an application does not enforce appropriate access controls or privilege separation, an attacker can exploit SQL injection vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data or perform unauthorized actions on the database.

questions.text: What does single page application means? Discuss about server side strategies.
questions.html: What does single page application means? Discuss about server side strategies.
questions.answerHtml:
A Single Page Application (SPA) is a web application that operates within a single web page, where the content dynamically updates without requiring a full page reload. In a SPA, the initial HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are loaded once, and subsequent interactions or data updates are handled through JavaScript, typically using APIs to retrieve or send data asynchronously. SPAs provide a more responsive and interactive user experience similar to that of a desktop application. They eliminate the need for full-page reloads, resulting in faster and smoother transitions between different views or components within the application.

Server-side strategies complement SPAs by handling tasks that are better suited for server-side processing or where security and privacy are concerns. Some server-side strategies commonly used in conjunction with SPAs include:

1. Authentication and Authorization: Server-side logic is responsible for managing user authentication, validating access tokens or cookies, and enforcing authorization rules. This ensures secure access to protected resources and prevents unauthorized access to sensitive data.

2. Data Validation and Business Logic: While client-side validation is crucial for a smooth user experience, serverside validation is essential for enforcing data integrity, ensuring consistency, and applying complex business rules that cannot be trusted to client-side code alone.

3. Data Persistence: Server-side components handle interactions with the database or other data sources, ensuring data consistency, data integrity, and managing transactions. They handle operations such as CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) and complex database queries.

questions.answerHtml:
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is an application-layer protocol used for communication between clients
(web browsers) and servers. It is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. HTTP defines how data is formatted and transmitted, and it specifies the actions that clients and servers should take to send and receive requests and responses. The MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern is a software architectural pattern commonly used in web development.

1. Model:

The Model represents the data and business logic of the application. It encapsulates the data, handles data validation and manipulation, and interacts with the database or external data sources. The Model is responsible for retrieving, storing, and manipulating the data required by the application.

2. View:

The View is responsible for presenting the user interface to the users. It defines how the data from the Model should be displayed and provides the necessary user interaction elements. The View is typically implemented using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in web applications.

3. Controller:

The Controller acts as an intermediary between the Model and the View. It receives user requests from the View, processes the requests, and interacts with the Model to retrieve or update the data. The Controller then updates the View with the updated data or triggers appropriate actions based on user input. It handles the logic and flow of the application.

questions.text: What does dependency injection and IOC container means? Explain.
questions.html: What does dependency injection and IOC container means? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
Dependency Injection (DI):

Dependency Injection is a design pattern that allows the dependencies of a class to be provided from the outside rather than being created within the class itself. It helps to remove the direct coupling between classes and makes them more flexible, maintainable, and testable. Instead of creating dependencies inside a class, they are “injected” from external sources. In DI, the dependencies are typically passed to a class through constructor parameters or setter methods. The class doesn’t need to know how to create or obtain its dependencies but relies on an external entity to provide them. This improves code reusability, and separation of concerns, and makes it easier to replace or modify dependencies without modifying the class itself.

Inversion of Control (IoC) Container:
An Inversion of Control (IoC) container is a software component or framework that implements the DI pattern and manages the creation and resolution of dependencies. It acts as a centralized container that holds the definitions of dependencies and resolves them when needed. IoC containers manage the lifecycle of objects, handle dependency resolution, and provide automatic dependency injection. They simplify the configuration and management of dependencies in an application by automatically wiring up the required dependencies based on predefined rules or configurations. IoC containers typically use reflection or configuration files to scan and analyze the application’s dependencies, construct objects, and inject the required dependencies automatically. Some popular IoC containers in the .NET ecosystem include Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, Autofac, and Unity.

In summary, Dependency Injection is a design pattern that allows dependencies to be provided from external sources, while an Inversion of Control container is a framework or component that manages the creation and injection of dependencies. Together, they promote loose coupling, and modular design, and make software more flexible and maintainable.

questions.text: Write short notes on (any two):  1. Lambda Expression  2. Containerization using Docker  3. Delegates and Events
questions.html:
Write short notes on (any two):

1. Lambda Expression

2. Containerization using Docker

3. Delegates and Events
questions.answerHtml:
1. Lambda Expression:

A Lambda expression is a concise way to define an anonymous function in programming. It allows you to write a block of code inline, without explicitly defining a separate method. Lambda expressions are often used in
functional programming and provide a more concise and readable syntax. They are especially useful when working with collections, LINQ queries, or when passing functions as parameters.

example:
int result = numbers.Sum(x => x * x);

In this example, the Lambda expression `x => x * x` represents a function that squares each element in the `numbers` collection and returns the sum of the squared values. It provides a shorter and more expressive way to define the operation.

2. Containerization using Docker:

Containerization is a method of packaging and running applications in a lightweight, isolated environment called a container. Docker is a popular containerization platform that allows you to create, deploy, and manage containers. Containers provide a consistent and portable environment for applications, ensuring that they can run reliably across different systems. Docker enables you to package an application along with its dependencies and configuration into a single container image. This image can be deployed on any system that has Docker installed, providing a consistent runtime environment. Containers offer benefits such as easy scalability, efficient resource utilization, and isolation of applications from the underlying infrastructure.
By using Docker, you can simplify the deployment process, improve application portability, and enable efficient utilization of resources in a consistent manner.

3. Delegates and Events:

Delegates and Events are concepts used in event-driven programming. A delegate is a type that represents a reference to a method. It allows you to treat methods as first-class objects, enabling you to pass methods as parameters, store them in variables, and invoke them dynamically. Delegates provide a way to define and work with callback functions. Events, on the other hand, are a language construct built on top of delegates. They provide a way to handle and respond to specific occurrences or actions, such as user interactions or system events. Events allow you to define and subscribe to event handlers, which are methods that are executed when the event is triggered.

For example, in C#, you can define an event like this:
public event EventHandler ButtonClicked;

This event indicates that a button click action can be subscribed to. Other parts of the code can then subscribe to this event and provide the corresponding event handler method that will be executed when the button is clicked.

Exception handling is an essential aspect of programming in C# because it allows you to easily handle unexpected or exceptional situations that can occur during the execution of a program. By handling exceptions, you can prevent your application from crashing or displaying cryptic error messages to the user. Instead, you can provide meaningful feedback and take appropriate actions to recover from the exceptional condition.

Console. class Program
{
static void Main()
{
try
{
int dividend = 10;
int divisor = 0;

Console.WriteLine(“Result: ” + result);
}

{

}

SQL Injection Attack Example:
SQL injection is a security vulnerability that occurs when an attacker can manipulate user-supplied input to execute arbitrary SQL commands on a database. To demonstrate the possibility of a SQL injection attack, here’s an example:

using System;
using System.Data.SqlClient;
class Program
{
static void Main()
{
Console.Write(“Enter a username: “);
string username = Console.ReadLine();
string connectionString = “your_connection_string”;
string query = $”SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Username = ‘{username}'”;
using (SqlConnection connection = new SqlConnection(connectionString))
{
connection.Open();
SqlCommand command = new SqlCommand(query, connection);
SqlDataReader reader = command.ExecuteReader();
while (reader.Read())
{
string userId = reader[“UserId”].ToString();
Console.WriteLine(“User ID: ” + userId);
}
}
}
}

In this example, we have a program that asks the user to enter a username. The program constructs a SQL query to retrieve the user’s ID from a database table called “Users” based on the provided username. However, this code is vulnerable to a SQL injection attack. An attacker can input malicious characters or SQL statements that modify the intended behaviour of the query. For example, an attacker can enter ‘ OR 1=1 — ‘ as the username, which would result in a query like:

SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Username = ‘ OR 1=1 –‘

In this case, the attacker’s intention is to retrieve all user records from the table by exploiting the `OR 1=1` condition, which is always true, and the — comments out the rest of the query. To prevent SQL injection attacks, it is crucial to use parameterized queries or stored procedures. Parameterized queries allow you to separate the SQL code from the user input, ensuring that the input is treated as data rather than executable code.

questions.answerHtml:
Open redirect attacks are a type of security vulnerability that occurs when a web application allows an attacker to redirect users to an arbitrary URL. This can be exploited by an attacker to trick users into visiting malicious websites or phishing pages, potentially leading to various types of attacks, such as stealing sensitive information, distributing malware, or gaining unauthorized access to user accounts. The vulnerability typically arises when a web application includes a parameter in the URL that determines the destination of a redirect. If this parameter can be manipulated by an attacker, they can change the redirect URL to an external site under their control.

Containers provide a consistent and portable environment for running applications across different computing environments, such as development, testing, and production.

Key aspects and benefits of Docker and containerization include:

– Containers provide process-level isolation, allowing applications to run independently of the host system and other containers.

– Containers are highly portable, as they package applications with their dependencies and configuration. This makes it easier to move applications between different environments, such as from a developer’s machine to a production server, without worrying about compatibility issues.

– Docker enables efficient scaling of applications by allowing you to run multiple containers across different hosts.

Named and positional attribute parameters refer to different ways of passing arguments to a function or method.

1. Positional Attribute Parameters: are defined based on their position or order in the function/method signature. When calling a function with positional attribute parameters, the arguments are passed in the same order as defined in the function signature. The values are matched to the corresponding parameters based on their position.

2. Named Attribute Parameters: are passed based on their parameter names rather than their positions. When calling a function with named attribute parameters, the arguments are specified with their corresponding parameter names, followed by an equals sign (=) and the argument value.

Figure: Net Framework Architecture Diagram

Net Framework Design Principle

The following design principles of the .Net framework are what make it very relevant to create .Net-based applications.

-Interoperability: The .Net framework provides a lot of backward support. Suppose you had an application built on an older version of the .Net framework, say 2.0. And if you tried to run the same application on a machine that had the higher version of the .Net framework, say 3.5. The application would still work. This is because, with every release, Microsoft ensures that older framework versions will get well with the latest version.

-Portability: Applications built on the .Net framework can be made to work on any Windows platform. And now in recent times, Microsoft is also envisioning making Microsft products work on other platforms, such as iOS and Linux.

-Security: The .Net framework has a good security mechanism. The inbuilt security mechanism helps in both validation and verification of applications. Every application can explicitly define its security mechanism. Each security mechanism is used to grant the user access to the code or to the running program.

-Memory Management: The common language runtime does all work or memory management. The .Net framework has all the capability to see those resources, which are not used by a running program. It would then release those resources accordingly. This is done via a program called the “Garbage Collector” which runs as part of the .Net framework. The garbage collector runs at regular intervals and keeps on checking which system resources are not utilized, and frees them accordingly.

questions.text: Why do we need to validate the form? How can you use react for this?
questions.html: Why do we need to validate the form? How can you use react for this?
questions.answerHtml:
Validating forms in .NET is important to ensure that the data submitted by users is accurate, complete, and meets the expected criteria. Form validation helps prevent data entry errors, improves the user experience by providing timely feedback, and enhances the overall integrity and security of the application. Form validation helps maintain data integrity by ensuring that the data entered by users conforms to the expected format and constraints. It prevents invalid or inconsistent data from being stored in the application’s database, avoiding issues with data quality. Proper form validation is also crucial for security purposes. It helps prevent common security vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and cross-site request forgery (CSRF). React provides a powerful and flexible way to handle form validation through its component-based architecture and state management. React provides various libraries and tools that can assist with form validation, such as Formik, Yup, or React Hook Form. These libraries offer additional features like form state management, validation schema, and error handling helpers, making the form validation process more streamlined and efficient.

An example of name validation in form is given below:
import React, { useState } from ‘react’;
const FormComponent = () => {
const [name, setName] = useState(”);
const [error, setError] = useState(”);
const handleSubmit = (e) => {
e.preventDefault();
if (!name.trim()) {
setError(‘Name is required’);
return;
}
console.log(‘Form submitted:’, { name });
};
return (
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
<input
type=”text”
placeholder=”Name”
value={name}
onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
/>
{error && <div className=”error”>{error}</div>}
<button type=”submit”>Submit</button>
</form>
); };
export default FormComponent;

questions.text: Define data model and data context. What does URL routing mean?
questions.html: Define data model and data context. What does URL routing mean?
questions.answerHtml:
Data Model:
A data model is a conceptual representation of how data is organized and structured within a system or application. It defines the relationships between data entities, their attributes, and the rules governing data manipulation and operations. Data models provide a blueprint for designing databases and serve as a foundation for data management and application development. Common types of data models include relational models, hierarchical models, network models, and object-oriented models.

Data Context:
In the context of software development, a data context refers to an object or component that encapsulates the connection and access to a specific data source, such as a database. The data context provides a convenient and centralized way to interact with the underlying data, including querying, inserting, updating, and deleting data. It simplifies data access and manipulation for application developers. In frameworks like Entity Framework in .NET, the data context is often represented by a DbContext class.

URL Routing:
URL routing refers to the process of mapping incoming URL requests to specific endpoints or resources within a web application. It enables the application to handle different URLs and route them to appropriate handlers or controllers, allowing for dynamic content generation and navigation. URL routing is commonly used in web frameworks and platforms to implement features like dynamic routing, parameterized URLs, and RESTful API routing. It is also used to generate outgoing URLs. This process is handled by the Routing Middleware. Routing Middleware is available in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing Namespace

questions.text: Give an example to manage the session state.
questions.html: Give an example to manage the session state.
questions.answerHtml:
Session state is an ASP.NET Core mechanism to store user data while the user browses the application. It uses a store maintained by the application to persist data across requests from a client.

Let’s create a controller with endpoints to set and read a value from the session:

public class WelcomemController : Controller

{

public IActionResult Index()

{

HttpContext.Session.SetString(“Name”,”John”);

HttpContext.Session.SetInt32(“Age”,32);

return View();

}

public IActionResult Get()

{

User newUser = new User()

{

Name = HttpContext.Session.GetString(“Name”),

Age = HttpContext.Sesssion.GetInt32(“Age”).Value

};

return View(newUser);

}

}

The Index() method sets the values into session and Get() method reads the values from the session and passes them into the view.

questions.text: How can you prevent SQL injection attack? Explain with an example.
questions.html: How can you prevent SQL injection attack? Explain with an example.
questions.answerHtml:
To prevent SQL injection attacks, it is essential to employ proper input validation and parameterization techniques.

Here’s an example to illustrate how to prevent SQL injection using parameterized queries in a .NET application

Consider a scenario where you have a login form that accepts a username and password to authenticate a user against a database. Without proper prevention mechanisms, an attacker could exploit the SQL injection vulnerability by entering a malicious input like `’ OR 1=1 –` in the username field, causing the SQL query to become:

SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Username = ” OR 1=1 –‘ AND Password = ‘enteredPassword’

This altered query could bypass the authentication logic, as the `OR 1=1` condition always evaluates to true, effectively ignoring the actual password check. To prevent SQL injection, you can use parameterized queries with prepared statements.

Here’s an example of how you can modify the code to use parameterized queries in C# with ADO.NET:

string username = // Get the username from the user input
string password = // Get the password from the user input
string query = “SELECT * FROM Users WHERE Username = @Username AND Password = @Password”;
using (SqlConnection connection = new SqlConnection(connectionString))
{
connection.Open();
using (SqlCommand command = new SqlCommand(query, connection))
{
command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“@Username”, username);
command.Parameters.AddWithValue(“@Password”, password);
// Execute the query and perform the necessary logic, such as checking if the user exists and if the password is correct
}

In this code, the query is parameterized by using placeholders like `@Username` and `@Password`. Instead of concatenating the user input directly into the SQL query, the `AddWithValue` method is used to bind the parameters securely. This ensures that the user input is treated as data and not as executable SQL code, thereby mitigating the risk of SQL injection.

questions.html: Explain the process to deploy the core application.
questions.answerHtml:
Some of the web servers that we can use to deploy our ASP.NET Core Application are:

-Microsoft IIS

-Apache

-NGINX

Steps to deploy ASP.NET Core to IIS

Before we deploy our application, we need to install the .NET Core hosting bundle for IIS – .NET Core runtime, libraries, and the ASP.NET Core module for IIS.

Step 1: Publish to a File Folder.

Step 2: Copy Files to the Preferred IIS Location.

For example, let’s copy the files to C:\inetpub\wwwroot\AspNetCore46

Step 3: Create an Application in IIS.

While creating an application in IIS is listed as a single “Step”, you will take multiple actions. First, create a new IIS Application Pool under the .NET CLR version of “No Managed Code”. Since IIS only works as a reverse proxy, it isn’t actually executing any .NET code. Second, you can create your application under an existing or a new IIS Site. Either way, you will want to pick your new IIS Application Pool and point it to the folder you copied your ASP.NET publish output files to.

Step 4: Load the App

questions.text: Write short notes on (any two)   a.LINQ  b. Open Redirected Attack  c. Query String
questions.html:
Write short notes on (any two)

a.LINQ

b. Open Redirected Attack

c. Query String
questions.answerHtml:
a) LINQ
LINQ (Language-Integrated Query) is a feature in .NET that allows developers to query and manipulate data using a unified syntax within the programming language. It provides a consistent way to work with data from various sources, such as databases, XML, collections, and more.

Here’s a simple example of LINQ using LINQ to Objects in .NET:

using System;
using System.Linq;
public class Program
{
public static void Main()
{
int[] numbers = { 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 };
// LINQ query expression
var evenNumbersQuery = from num in numbers where num % 2 == 0 select num;
var evenNumbers = evenNumbersQuery.ToList();
// Display the results
Console.WriteLine(“Even Numbers:”);
foreach (var num in evenNumbers)
{
Console.WriteLine(num);
}
}
}

b) Open Redirected Attacks

Open redirect attacks are a type of security vulnerability that occurs when a web application allows an attacker to redirect users to an arbitrary URL. This can be exploited by an attacker to trick users into visiting malicious websites or phishing pages, potentially leading to various types of attacks, such as stealing sensitive information, distributing malware, or gaining unauthorized access to user accounts. The vulnerability typically arises when a web application includes a parameter in the URL that determines the destination of a redirect. If this parameter can be manipulated by an attacker, they can change the redirect URL to an external site under their control.

c) Query String
In .NET, a query string refers to the portion of a URL that contains data in the form of key-value pairs. It is typically used to pass information from a client (such as a web browser) to a server. The query string is appended to the URL and starts with a question mark “?” followed by one or more key-value pairs separated by ampersands “&”.

Here’s a simple example in .NET to illustrate the usage of a query string:

using System;
class Program
{
static void Main()
{
string url = “http://example.com/page?param1=value1&param2=value2”;
// Parse the query string
var query = new System.Uri(url).Query;
var queryParams = System.Web.HttpUtility.ParseQueryString(query);
// Retrieve values from the query string
string param1 = queryParams[“param1”];
string param2 = queryParams[“param2”];
// Display the values
Console.WriteLine(“param1: ” + param1);
Console.WriteLine(“param2: ” + param2);
}
}
In this example, we start with a sample URL that contains a query string:
`http://example.com/page?param1=value1&param2=value2`.

questions.text: List different stakeholders involved in software inspection. How software inspection is carried out? Explain
questions.html: List different stakeholders involved in software inspection. How software inspection is carried out? Explain
questions.answerHtml:
Software inspection is a control technique that ensures the documentation produced during a given phase remains consistent with the documentation of the previous phases and respects the established rules and standards. It involves people examining the source representation of the software to discover anomalies and defects. The aim of an inspection is to locate faults, and the process is driven by a fault checklist.

The stakeholders involved in a software inspection are as follows:

a) Author: The author is the person who created the work product being inspected. The author is responsible for producing the documents and fixing the defects found.

b) Moderator: The moderator is the leader of the inspection. The moderator plans the inspection and coordinates it.

c) Chief moderator: The chief moderator is responsible for improving the inspection process and for updating the checklist.

d) Reader: The reader reads through the documents one item at a time. The reader presents the code or documents at the inspection meeting.

e) Inspector: The inspector examines the work product to identify possible defects and find errors.

Second Part;

The inspection is carried out in the following steps:

a) Planning: The moderator plans the inspection. This involves selecting an inspection team and organizing a meeting room and the materials.

b) Overview: The software and the documents to be inspected are presented to the inspection team.

c) Individual preparation: Each member of the inspection team studies the specification and the program on their own and looks for defects.

d) Inspection meeting: The readers read through the work product part by part, and the inspectors point out the defects found in every part.

e) Rework: The author changes the work product according to the action plan that came out of the inspection meeting.

f) Follow-up: The changes made by the author are checked to make sure that everything is correct. The moderator decides whether the code and documents need to be inspected again. If not, the moderator approves the software for release.

questions.text: List some advantages of estimation. Explain COCOMO mode
questions.html: List some advantages of estimation. Explain COCOMO model.
questions.answerHtml:
Software estimation is the process of estimating the size of the software product, the effort required and the overall cost of the project. The advantages of estimation are as follows:

a) Financial planning: Estimation helps in planning the financial side of the project, which helps to avoid financial shortfalls.

b) Resource planning: It makes sure the necessary resources are identified and allocated accordingly.

c) Timeline creation: It helps in developing realistic timelines and milestones for the project.

d) Identifying risks: It helps to identify the potential risks of carrying out the project.

e) Detailed planning: It supports a detailed plan for executing the project in which all aspects of the project are considered.

f) Planning quality assurance: It helps in planning quality assurance activities so that the outcomes meet the required standards.

COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) is a widely used software cost estimation model developed by Barry Boehm in the late 1970s and later extended and refined. COCOMO provides a framework for estimating the effort, time, and resources required to develop a software project based on various factors such as project size, complexity, and development environment. COCOMO is based on empirical data collected from numerous software projects and has evolved into several versions to accommodate different development environments and project characteristics.

In COCOMO, projects are categorised into three types:

a) Organic: The team size is adequately small, and the problem is well understood and has been solved in the past. Examples are simple business systems, simple inventory management systems and data processing systems.

b) Semi-detached: The development team consists of a mixture of experienced and inexperienced staff. Examples are developing a new operating system, a database management system or a complex inventory management system.

c) Embedded: The project requires the highest level of complexity, creativity and experience. Examples are an ATM and air traffic control.

There are three main versions of the COCOMO model:

  1. Basic COCOMO (COCOMO I): Basic COCOMO is the original version of the model and is primarily used for early-stage rough estimates of software projects. It estimates software development effort as a function of the project size measured in lines of code (LOC). The formula for Basic COCOMO is as follows: Effort (E) = a * (KLOC)b Where:
    • E is the effort required to develop the software project.
    • KLOC is the estimated size of the software project in thousands of lines of code.
    • a and b are constants derived from historical data and depend on the project type and development environment.
  2.  Intermediate COCOMO (COCOMO II): Intermediate COCOMO extends the basic model by incorporating additional factors that influence software development effort and cost. It introduces different cost drivers that affect the overall project effort, including product, platform, personnel, project, and process attributes. These cost drivers are categorized into various factors such as product complexity, development environment, team experience, and project constraints. The formula for Intermediate COCOMO is more complex than Basic COCOMO and accounts for these additional factors.
  3. Detailed COCOMO (COCOMO III): Detailed COCOMO is the most comprehensive version of the model and provides a detailed breakdown of effort estimation by considering individual software development activities and phases. It takes into account factors such as software requirements, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance. Detailed COCOMO allows for a more fine-grained estimation of effort and resources based on specific project characteristics and development methodologies.

questions.text: Why do you think software needs to be changed? Explain any one model that can be used to cope with the change.
questions.html: Why do you think software needs to be changed? Explain any one model that can be used to cope with the change.
questions.answerHtml:
The modification of software to meet new, corrected or improved needs, during development and after delivery, is known as software change. Change is certain in all large software projects, so software must be written in a way that lets it evolve. The main reasons why software needs to change are as follows:

a) Changing business requirements: System requirements change as businesses respond to external pressures, competition and changed management priorities. For example, an online shopping system in Nepal may need to add a new payment option such as Khalti when customers start asking for it.

b) Changing customer needs over time: The needs of customers evolve with time, so software must be maintainable and written in a way that lets it evolve with them. Software that cannot change soon becomes useless.

c) Requirements not clear at the start: Customers often cannot state exactly what they want in the beginning. After they experiment with the delivered system, they clarify their requirements and ask for changes in later versions.

d) Fixing errors after delivery: Defects and issues are found once the product is deployed in the customer environment, so maintenance is needed to fix them.

e) Enhancing the product: Maintenance is also done to improve the product into better versions with new or improved features.

f) Updating legacy software: Old software must be maintained and updated so that essential business services continue to be delivered without excessive cost.

Change adds to the cost of development because work that has already been completed usually has to be redone. A software process therefore needs a way to cope with change. Two such ways are prototyping and incremental delivery, and the prototyping model is explained below.

In the prototyping model, developers do not spend a lot of time producing very detailed specifications. They find out only an outline of the system and quickly build a prototype containing some portions of it. This prototype is refined and extended iteratively until the final specification is reached. The model is used when requirements are not clear or well understood, so that changes are discovered early and cheaply. The figure below shows the model.

The Prototyping Model is a software development model in which a working prototype is developed quickly and shown to the customer. The customer provides feedback, and the requirements and prototype are refined repeatedly until the requirements are clearly understood and accepted.

Working of the Prototyping Model

The working of the model is as follows:

a) Requirements Gathering:
Only the basic outline of the system’s requirements is collected from the customer, rather than a complete and detailed specification.

b) Quick Design:
A simple and rapid design is prepared for the parts of the system that the customer will see and use.

c) Build Prototype:
A working prototype containing some parts of the system is quickly developed based on the quick design.

d) Customer Evaluation of Prototype:
The customer uses and evaluates the prototype and provides suggestions and feedback.

e) Refine Requirements:
The customer’s feedback is used to refine the requirements. The quick design and prototype are updated accordingly. This cycle is repeated until the customer is satisfied with and accepts the prototype.

f) Design, Implement, Test and Maintain:
After the final requirements are agreed upon, the actual system is designed, implemented, tested and maintained.

Types of Prototyping

Prototyping is mainly of two types:

i) Evolutionary Prototyping:
In evolutionary prototyping, the initial prototype is continuously refined based on customer feedback until it becomes the final accepted system. It saves time and effort because the prototype is improved instead of creating a new one from scratch. It is suitable for projects using new technology and projects where requirements are unclear or unstable at the beginning.

ii) Throw-away Prototyping:
In throw-away prototyping, a quick prototype is developed based on the preliminary requirements and shown to the customer. The customer provides feedback, the requirements are changed, and new prototypes may be created until the requirements are clearly understood and fixed. The prototype is then discarded and is not used as part of the final system. It is useful for exploring ideas and obtaining quick customer feedback.

Benefits of Prototyping in Coping with Change
  • Misunderstood or changing requirements can be identified before the complete system is developed.
  • The cost and effort of making changes later are reduced.
  • Customers get a clearer understanding of the proposed system.
  • Continuous customer feedback reduces the risk of developing software that does not meet customer needs.
  • It helps identify missing requirements and design problems at an early stage.

e) Enhancing the product: Maintenance is also done to improve the product into better versions with new or improved features.

f) Updating legacy software: Old software must be maintained and updated so that essential business services continue to be delivered without excessive cost.

Change adds to the cost of development because work that has already been completed usually has to be redone. A software process therefore needs a way to cope with change. Two such ways are prototyping and incremental delivery, and the prototyping model is explained below.

In the prototyping model, developers do not spend a lot of time producing very detailed specifications. They find out only an outline of the system and quickly build a prototype containing some portions of it. This prototype is refined and extended iteratively until the final specification is reached. The model is used when requirements are not clear or well understood, so that changes are discovered early and cheaply. The figure below shows the model.

The Prototyping Model is a software development model in which a working prototype is developed quickly and shown to the customer. The customer provides feedback, and the requirements and prototype are refined repeatedly until the requirements are clearly understood and accepted.

Working of the Prototyping Model
The working of the model is as follows:

a) Requirements Gathering:

Only the basic outline of the system’s requirements is collected from the customer, rather than a complete and detailed specification.

b) Quick Design:

A simple and rapid design is prepared for the parts of the system that the customer will see and use.

c) Build Prototype:

A working prototype containing some parts of the system is quickly developed based on the quick design.

d) Customer Evaluation of Prototype:

The customer uses and evaluates the prototype and provides suggestions and feedback.

e) Refine Requirements:

The customer’s feedback is used to refine the requirements. The quick design and prototype are updated accordingly. This cycle is repeated until the customer is satisfied with and accepts the prototype.

f) Design, Implement, Test and Maintain:

After the final requirements are agreed upon, the actual system is designed, implemented, tested and maintained.

Types of Prototyping
Prototyping is mainly of two types:

i) Evolutionary Prototyping:

In evolutionary prototyping, the initial prototype is continuously refined based on customer feedback until it becomes the final accepted system. It saves time and effort because the prototype is improved instead of creating a new one from scratch. It is suitable for projects using new technology and projects where requirements are unclear or unstable at the beginning.

ii) Throw-away Prototyping:

In throw-away prototyping, a quick prototype is developed based on the preliminary requirements and shown to the customer. The customer provides feedback, the requirements are changed, and new prototypes may be created until the requirements are clearly understood and fixed. The prototype is then discarded and is not used as part of the final system. It is useful for exploring ideas and obtaining quick customer feedback.

Benefits of Prototyping in Coping with Change

Misunderstood or changing requirements can be identified before the complete system is developed.

The cost and effort of making changes later are reduced.

Customers get a clearer understanding of the proposed system.

Continuous customer feedback reduces the risk of developing software that does not meet customer needs.

It helps identify missing requirements and design problems at an early stage.

questions.text: Describe software engineering ethics thal needs to be followed.Why is it important ?
questions.html: Describe software engineering ethics thal needs to be followed.Why is it important ?
questions.answerHtml:
Software engineering ethics are the moral principles and professional responsibilities that software engineers follow while developing and maintaining software. Software engineering is more than technical work, because the software affects clients, employers, users and society. Engineers must therefore behave honestly and responsibly.

The main ethical principles are as follows:

a) Confidentiality: Engineers should normally respect the confidentiality of their employers and clients, whether or not a formal confidentiality agreement has been signed. For example, a developer working on a payment app for an eSewa-like service must not leak customer data or business secrets.

b) Competence: Engineers should never misrepresent their level of skill. They should not accept work that is beyond their competence, since poor work from an unqualified person harms the client and the quality of the product.

c) Intellectual property rights: Engineers should know the local laws governing the use of intellectual property such as patents and copyright. They must protect the intellectual property of employers and clients, and must not copy or use others’ code illegally.

d) Computer misuse: Engineers should not use their technical skills to misuse other people’s computers. Misuse ranges from minor cases, such as playing games on an employer’s machine, to extremely serious ones, such as spreading viruses.

These ethics are important for the following reasons:

i) Society depends on software: The economies of developed nations depend on software, and more and more systems are software controlled. Unethical practice can therefore harm a very large number of people.

ii) Trust of clients and users: When engineers keep information confidential and work honestly, clients and users can trust them and the software they build.

iii) Quality and reliability: Working only within one’s competence leads to dependable software with fewer failures, which matters most in safety-critical systems.

iv) Legal protection: Respecting intellectual property rights and avoiding computer misuse keeps engineers and organizations out of legal trouble such as copyright disputes and cybercrime cases.

v) Professional reputation: Ethical conduct builds the reputation of the engineer, the company and the software engineering profession as a whole.

questions.text: Differentiate between plan driven and agile development. Explain agile project management.
questions.html: Differentiate between plan driven and agile development. Explain agile project management.
questions.answerHtml:
Basis Plan-driven development Agile development
Planning All process activities are planned in advance, and progress is measured against this plan. Planning is incremental, so it is easier to change the plan and software to reflect changing customer requirements.
Iteration Iteration occurs within activities. Iteration occurs across activities.
When it is used Used when a very detailed specification and design are available. Used when very limited planning is required to get started with the project.
Skill level required Sometimes requires lower skill levels than the agile approach. Sometimes requires higher skill levels than the plan-driven approach.
Suitability More suitable for large systems. More suitable for smaller systems.

Agile project management is the way of managing a software project in which requirements are developed incrementally and delivered at short time intervals. A software project manager must deliver the software on time and within the estimated budget. Traditionally this is done through a plan-based approach, which needs a stable view of everything that has to be developed. This does not fit agile methods, so a different approach to project management is used, and it is realized in Scrum.

The main points are as follows:

a) Need for a different approach: In agile methods the requirements change and are delivered in small increments. Project management therefore has to support incremental development and the strengths of agile methods rather than a fixed plan.

b) Scrum framework: Scrum is an iterative and incremental agile software development framework for managing agile software projects.

c) Small interdependent teams: Scrum is based on multiple small teams working in an intensive and interdependent manner.

d) Development in small pieces: The product is developed in small pieces, and each piece builds on the previously created pieces. In standard Scrum these pieces are built in fixed short cycles called sprints.

questions.text: What do you understand by model driven architecture? Explain.
questions.html: What do you understand by model driven architecture? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
Model-driven architecture (MDA) is an approach to software design and implementation that focuses on developing models rather than writing code first. It uses UML models to describe a system, and models at different levels of abstraction are created.

MDA recommends that three types of abstract system model should be produced:

a) Computation independent model (CIM): It models the important domain abstractions used in a system, so it is sometimes called a domain model. Several different CIMs can be developed to reflect different views of the system.

b) Platform-independent model (PIM): It models the operation of the system without any reference to its implementation. A PIM is usually described using UML models that show the static system structure and how the system responds to external and internal events.

c) Platform-specific model (PSM): It is a transformation of the platform-independent model, with a separate PSM for each application platform. In principle there may be layers of PSM, with each layer adding some platform-specific detail.

Advantages: It allows systems to be considered at a higher level of abstraction. Because code can be generated automatically, it is cheaper to adapt systems to new platforms.

Disadvantages: Models are meant for abstraction and are not necessarily right for implementation. The savings from generating code may be outweighed by the cost of developing translators for new platforms.

questions.text: What are the issues that may occur while implementation? How can these issues be handled?
questions.html: What are the issues that may occur while implementation? How can these issues be handled?
questions.answerHtml:
Implementation is the process of realizing the design as a program, that is, turning the design model into a working product. The aspects of this stage that cause problems are called implementation issues, and the main ones are reuse, configuration management and host-target development.

The issues that may occur are:

a) Reuse: Modern software is built by reusing existing components or systems, but this has drawbacks. Old components may fail to do their functions, which raises the maintenance cost. Tools used earlier may need longer support or may become obsolete. Selecting a component that can be used for the long term takes time. If one component fails, the interconnected components also fail, and the whole system can fail.

b) Configuration management: Many different versions of each software component are created during development. It becomes easy to lose track of which changes and component versions are included in each version of the system.

c) Host-target development: The software is developed on one computer, the host, but runs on a separate computer, the target. Software that works on the development computer may not work correctly on the target computer.

These issues can be handled in the following ways:

a) Handling reuse issues: Reuse is done at a suitable level, namely the object level, the component level or the system level. Time is given to selecting components that will last, and the tools of reused components are kept up to date and supported. Reused components should be tested before they are integrated.

b) Handling configuration management issues: A configuration management system keeps track of the versions of every component. It lets all developers access the project code and documents in a controlled way, find out what changes were made, and link the components to create a system. It works through change management, version management, system building and release management.

c) Handling host-target issues: The software is installed and tested on the target computer, or on a simulator of it, before release. Any differences between the host and target environments are found and fixed at that stage.

questions.text: Explain the process of release resting and user testing.
questions.html: Explain the process of release resting and user testing.
questions.answerHtml:
The testing of a system release before it goes to customers is called release testing, and the stage in which users or customers take part in testing the system is called user testing. Both are explained below.

Release testing proceeds as follows:

  • Purpose of release testing: It refers to coding practices and test strategies that give the team confidence that a software release candidate is ready for users. A release candidate is the version of the system that is intended to be given to customers.
  • Finding errors in the release: It aims to find and eliminate errors and bugs from the release so that it can be handed over to users.
  • Convincing the customer: The primary goal of release testing is to convince the customer that the system is good enough for use. A release that passes the tests is therefore accepted for delivery.
  • How it is carried out: The complete system is tested as a black box against its specified requirements by a team separate from the developers. The tests include checking each requirement, running typical usage scenarios and checking performance.

User testing proceeds as follows:

  • Purpose of user testing: It is the stage in the testing process in which users or customers provide input and advice on system testing. Their feedback shows whether the system really works in their situation.
  • Why it is essential: It is needed even when comprehensive system and release testing have been carried out. The influences of the user’s working environment have a major effect on the reliability, performance, usability and robustness of a system, and these cannot be replicated in a testing environment.
  • Alpha testing: This is done to identify bugs before the product is released to real users, and it is typically done by QA people.
  • Beta testing: A version of the system is released to a limited number of users who test it in a real-time environment. The bugs they report are fixed before the final release.
  • Acceptance testing: The customer checks whether the system meets the specified requirements, and on this basis decides whether to accept it. Alpha and beta testing are its two types.

questions.text: Define software maintenance. Explain the software maintenance process.
questions.html: Define software maintenance. Explain the software maintenance process.
questions.answerHtml:
Software maintenance is the activity of modifying a software system after it has been delivered. It includes optimization, error correction, deletion of discarded features and enhancement of existing features. Maintenance does not normally involve major changes to the architecture of the system. The changes are made by modifying existing components and by adding new components to the system.

The software maintenance process consists of four major activities:

a) Obtaining maintenance requests: A formal process is established through which users can submit change requests for the system. This gives all changes a proper starting point and a record.

b) Transforming requests into changes: Once a request is received, it is analysed to identify its scope. The analysis determines how the request will affect the current system and how long such a project will take.

c) Designing changes: An approved change request is transformed into a formal design change, which is then fed into the maintenance phase.

d) Implementing changes: Once the change design is approved, the proposed changes are implemented in the respective components of the system.

Types of maintenance carried out: Through these activities, the following types of maintenance are performed:
i) Corrective maintenance repairs faults or defects found in the design, coding or implementation of the system.
ii) Adaptive maintenance makes changes in one part of the system that has been affected by a change in some other part.
iii) Perfective maintenance makes functional enhancements to the system to increase its performance.
iv) Preventive maintenance performs activities to prevent errors from occurring.

questions.text: Explain the steps that are carried out during configuration management.
questions.html: Explain the steps that are carried out during configuration management.
questions.answerHtml:
Configuration management is concerned with the policies, processes and tools for managing a changing software system. It is essential because it is easy to lose track of which changes and component versions have been included in each version of the system. The activities carried out in it are as follows:

a) Change management: This keeps track of changes to the system. A change request is submitted and evaluated for its technical merit, possible side effects, effect on other components and cost. A change control board then decides whether the change is accepted and how important it is. For an approved change, the component is checked out, changed, tested again and checked back in.

b) Version management: This keeps track of the many different versions of each software component in the configuration management system. Each change creates a new version, for example from version 1.0 to 1.1 for a small change, and a major change leads to a new version such as 2.0.

c) System building: This is the process of linking components together to create a system. The correct versions of the components, together with libraries and configuration files, are compiled and linked to produce a complete, executable system.

d) Release management: A system release is a version of the system that is distributed to customers. This activity prepares the chosen version for delivery to customers and keeps track of which versions have been released.

e) Support for system integration: The aim of these activities is to support the system integration process. All developers can access the project code and documents in a controlled way, find out what changes have been made, and link components to create a system.

f) Configuration auditing and reporting: An audit checks that the modified items are complete, correct and consistent. Reporting then gives developers, testers and customers accurate information on the current status of the configuration.

questions.text: Explain the requirement engineering process.
questions.html: Explain the requirement engineering process.
questions.answerHtml:
The requirements engineering process involves all the activities required to create and maintain a system requirements document. Its purpose is to make the stated problem clear and complete, and to ensure that the solution is correct, reasonable and effective. The exact process varies with the application domain, the people involved and the organization developing the requirements, but the following activities are common to all processes:

a) Feasibility study: Resource availability, the cost estimate for development, the benefits the organization will get from the software, and the cost of its maintenance are studied to decide whether the system is worth building. It has three parts:
i) Technical feasibility checks whether the hardware and software needed to meet the user requirements are available within the allocated time and budget.
ii) Economic feasibility determines whether the software can generate financial gains for the organization.
iii) Operational feasibility checks how well the software performs the series of steps needed to solve the user requirements.

b) Requirements elicitation and analysis: Requirements are gathered from users, customers and other stakeholders and then analysed. It consists of four main activities:
i) Requirements discovery is interacting with stakeholders to gather their requirements for the required system and the existing system.
ii) Requirements classification and organization puts related requirements together and decomposes the system into sub-components of related requirements.
iii) Requirements prioritization and negotiation ranks the requirements and resolves conflicts between them through negotiation until stakeholders can compromise.
iv) Requirements specification checks the requirements for completeness and consistency and documents them as input to the next round of the spiral.

c) Requirements specification: The management of the organization studies the feasibility report and suggests modifications to the requirements, if any. Considering the constraints on available resources and the modified requirements, the system analyst draws up the final specification of the system to be developed.

d) Requirements validation: The requirements are checked for validity, consistency, completeness, realism and verifiability. This shows that the requirements really define the system the customer wants. It is carried out through checks such as the validity check, completeness check and consistency check.

e) Requirements change management: This is the process of understanding and controlling changes to the system requirements. It is essential because the benefits of implementing a new requirement must be weighed against the cost of implementing it.

questions.text: Write short notes on  a. Project scheduling  b. Internet software engineering
questions.html:
Write short notes on

a. Project scheduling

b. Internet software engineering
questions.answerHtml:
a)Project scheduling

Project scheduling is the process of dividing the total work of a software project into separate activities and judging the time needed to complete each one. The result is a detailed plan showing when each activity should start and finish, and when and how much resource will be needed. Creating a project schedule involves four stages: constructing an ideal activity plan, risk analysis, resource allocation and schedule production.

Schedules are usually shown as a set of charts that give the work breakdown, the dependencies between activities and the staff allocation. Bar charts such as the Gantt chart show who is responsible for each activity and when it begins and ends. Activity networks show the dependencies between the different activities. Scheduling is also one section of the project plan, where it shows how the activities depend on each other.

b)Internet software engineering

Internet software engineering is the development of software that runs over the Internet instead of on a local system. The Internet is now a platform for running applications, and Internet services allow an application’s functionality to be accessed over the Internet.

With this approach, the software is developed and deployed on a web server and users reach it through their browsers, instead of installing it on each PC. This makes it much cheaper to change and upgrade the software, because it does not have to be updated on every user’s PC. A bank’s web portal that customers open from any computer is a common example.

questions.text: What is software testing? Explain the software testing process in detail. Differentiate between development testing and release testing. How does Test-Driven Development (TDD) improve software quality? Explain with an example.
questions.html: What is software testing? Explain the software testing process in detail. Differentiate between development testing and release testing. How does Test-Driven Development (TDD) improve software quality? Explain with an example.
questions.answerHtml:
Software testing is intended to show that a program does what it is intended to do and to discover program defects before it is put into use. When we test software, we execute a program using artificial data. We check the results of the test run for errors, anomalies or information about the program’s non-functional attributes.

Program testing goals:

➤ To demonstrate to the developer and the customer that the software meets its requirements.

➤ To discover situations in which the behavior of the software is incorrect.

Software Testing Process:


Software testing process starts with preparation of test cases. Test cases are specification of the inputs to the test and the expected output from the system together with what is being tested. From the design of test cases we get test case list. After that we prepare the test data. Test data are the inputs which have been designed to test the system. Test data can be generated automatically or manually. From this step we get test data set. Then we run the program with test data for all test cases and generate the result. Finally, we compare the test result to test cases and generate the test report.

Difference between development testing and release testing are as follows:

S.No Development Testing Release Testing
1 Performed during the software development life cycle Performed after development is completed, before release
2 Ensures detection of bugs or errors at the right time to reduce risk and cost Ensures that the final software is ready for users
3 Focuses on verifying whether requirements are met during development Focuses on finding and removing remaining bugs and errors before release
4 Aims to establish a framework to ensure compliance with project rules Aims to build confidence that the release candidate is usable
5 Performed by software developers or engineers during construction phase Performed by testing teams to assure quality for end users

How Test-Driven Development (TDD) Improves Software Quality:

Test-Driven Development (TDD) is an approach to program development in which we interleave testing and code development. In TDD, tests are written before the actual code, and passing these tests is the critical driver of development. This methodology significantly improves software quality through several key mechanisms.

TDD improves software quality by ensuring that every piece of code has a corresponding test before it’s even written. This forces developers to think about requirements and expected behavior upfront, leading to clearer specifications and better-designed code. Since tests are created first, developers write only the minimum code necessary to pass those tests, resulting in cleaner, more focused implementations with less unnecessary complexity. The iterative nature of TDD—where code is developed incrementally along with tests for each increment—catches bugs early in the development cycle when they’re cheaper and easier to fix.

Additionally, TDD creates a comprehensive test suite that acts as a safety net for future changes. When modifications or refactoring are needed, the existing tests immediately verify that new changes haven’t broken existing functionality. This reduces regression bugs and increases confidence in code changes. The practice also improves code maintainability because well-tested code is typically better structured and more modular.
