questions.text: Why is it necessary to implement E-Governance to provide government services to citizens efficiently and effectively? Explain using suitable example.
questions.html: Why is it necessary to implement E-Governance to provide government services to citizens efficiently and effectively? Explain using suitable example.
questions.answerHtml:
Implementing e-governance is necessary to provide government services to citizens efficiently and effectively due to several reasons. One suitable example to illustrate this is the implementation of an online portal for citizen registration and issuance of identification documents.

In a traditional, non-digitized system, citizens would typically have to visit multiple government offices, fill out numerous forms, and submit various documents to obtain identification documents such as a national ID card or a passport. This process is time-consuming, requires physical presence, and often involves long waiting times.

However, with the implementation of e-governance, citizens can access a centralized online portal where they can register for identification documents and submit the required information and documents electronically. The portal can have user-friendly interfaces and guides to assist citizens in completing the necessary steps. Through the portal, citizens can upload digital copies of their documents, provide the required personal information, and track the progress of their applications.

By implementing e-governance in this scenario, several benefits are achieved:

  • Efficiency: The online portal streamlines the process, reducing the need for physical visits to multiple government offices. Citizens can complete the application at their convenience, saving time and effort. The automation of document verification and application processing also speeds up the overall process.
  • Convenience: Citizens can access the online portal from anywhere with internet connectivity, eliminating geographical constraints. They can submit applications outside of traditional office hours, avoiding the need to take time off from work or other obligations. The portal offers a convenient and accessible platform for citizens to interact with the government and access services.
  • Transparency: Through the online portal, citizens can track the status of their application and receive notifications or updates on the progress. This enhances transparency and eliminates the uncertainty associated with traditional paper-based processes. Citizens have clear visibility into the process and can easily inquire about any delays or issues.
  • Accuracy and Data Integrity: E-governance systems can have built-in validation checks to ensure that citizens provide accurate and complete information during the application process. This reduces errors, enhances data integrity, and minimizes the need for manual data entry by government officials. The use of digital documents and data also reduces the risk of document loss or tampering.

By implementing e-governance, the process of obtaining identification documents becomes efficient, convenient, transparent, and accurate. This example demonstrates how e-governance improves the delivery of government services, simplifies procedures for citizens, and enhances the overall citizen experience. It showcases the potential for digital platforms to revolutionize traditional bureaucratic processes and make government services more citizen-centric and accessible.

Through the portal, citizens can upload digital copies of their documents, provide the required personal information, and track the progress of their applications.

By implementing e-governance in this scenario, several benefits are achieved:

Efficiency: The online portal streamlines the process, reducing the need for physical visits to multiple government offices. Citizens can complete the application at their convenience, saving time and effort. The automation of document verification and application processing also speeds up the overall process.

Convenience: Citizens can access the online portal from anywhere with internet connectivity, eliminating geographical constraints. They can submit applications outside of traditional office hours, avoiding the need to take time off from work or other obligations. The portal offers a convenient and accessible platform for citizens to interact with the government and access services.

Transparency: Through the online portal, citizens can track the status of their application and receive notifications or updates on the progress. This enhances transparency and eliminates the uncertainty associated with traditional paper-based processes. Citizens have clear visibility into the process and can easily inquire about any delays or issues.

Accuracy and Data Integrity: E-governance systems can have built-in validation checks to ensure that citizens provide accurate and complete information during the application process. This reduces errors, enhances data integrity, and minimizes the need for manual data entry by government officials. The use of digital documents and data also reduces the risk of document loss or tampering.

By implementing e-governance, the process of obtaining identification documents becomes efficient, convenient, transparent, and accurate. This example demonstrates how e-governance improves the delivery of government services, simplifies procedures for citizens, and enhances the overall citizen experience. It showcases the potential for digital platforms to revolutionize traditional bureaucratic processes and make government services more citizen-centric and accessible.

questions.text: Why do we need E-Governance model? Explain comparative analysis model, and mobilization and lobbying model in detail.
questions.html: Why do we need E-Governance model? Explain comparative analysis model, and mobilization and lobbying model in detail.
questions.answerHtml:
E-governance models are essential to enhance the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of government operations. It promotes citizen engagement and participation by providing opportunities for feedback, consultation, and involvement in decision-making processes. Additionally, these models improve the accessibility of government services, especially for individuals in remote or underserved areas.  e-governance models transform the way governments operate, making them more efficient, transparent, and responsive to citizen needs.

Comparative Analysis Model

  • The Comparative Analysis Model is based on exploring information available in the public or private domain and comparing it with the actual known information sets to derive strategic learnings and arguments.
  • This model empowers people by comparing cases of bad governance with those of good governance and identifying specific aspects of bad governance, the reasons and people behind them, and how the situation can be improved.
  • The comparison could be made over a time scale to get a snapshot of the past and the present situation or could be used to compare the effectiveness of an intervention by comparing two similar situations.

Applications:

  • To learn from past policies and actions and derive learning lessons for future policy-making.
  • To evaluate the effectiveness of the current policies and identify key learning in terms of strengths and flaws in the policies.
  • To effectively establish conditions of precedence, especially in the case of Judicial or legal decision-making (for resolving patent-related disputes, public goods ownership rights), and use it to influence/ advocate future decision-making.
  • To evaluate the performance and track record of a particular decision-maker/decision-making body.

Merits :

  • Based on the existing sets of information
  • Watch-guard organizations and monitor groups can use this model to continuously track the governance past record and performance and compare with different information sets.

Demerits :

  • Requires the ability to analyze and bring out strong arguments
  • Ineffective in the absence of a strong civil society interest and public memory which is essential to force decision-makers to improve existing governance practices

Mobilization and Lobbying Model

  • Mobilisation and Lobbying Model is one of the most frequently used digital governance models and has often come to the aid of civil society organizations in developing countries to impact international decision-making processes.
  • It is based on setting up a planned, directed flow of information to build strong virtual allies to complement actions in the real world.
  • Virtual communities are formed which share similar values and concerns, and these communities in turn link up with or support real-life groups/ activities for concerted action.
  • It builds the momentum of real-world processes by adding the opinions and concerns expressed by virtual communities.
  • The strength of this model is in its diversity of the virtual community, and the ideas, expertise and resources accumulated through this virtual form of networking.

Applications:

  • This model could be applied in the following possible ways:
  • Fostering public debates on issues of larger concern, namely on the themes of upcoming conferences, treaties, etc.
  • Making available opinions of suppressed groups who are not involved in the decision-making process into the wider public domain.
  • Catalyzing wider participation in decision-making processes.

Merits :

  • The model enhances the scope of participation of individuals and communities in debates that affect them and help them build a global alliance.
  • A community may no longer find itself isolated but may find an ally for mobilizing effective action through this model.
  • It also creates an effective deterrent for governments and decision-making bodies that are responsive to people’s opinions to provide better governance.
  • The model could also be used favorably by the government in a positive manner to encourage public debates on issues where the opinion and expertise of civil society is of great importance and therefore could become a tool to enhance democratic practices and improve governance practices (especially in Developing Countries).

questions.text: Why is it necessary to have IT infrastructure to implement E-Government? Explain different IT infrastructure needed to implement E-government.
questions.html: Why is it necessary to have IT infrastructure to implement E-Government? Explain different IT infrastructure needed to implement E-government.
questions.answerHtml:
IT infrastructure is crucial for the implementation of e-governance because it forms the backbone of digital transformation and enables governments to deliver efficient and accessible services to citizens. It supports the development of digital platforms, websites, and applications through which citizens can access government information and interact with services.

Additionally, IT infrastructure facilitates the collection, storage, processing, and analysis of data, ensuring its security, privacy, and integrity. It also provides the necessary connectivity and communication channels for government entities to collaborate, share information, and engage with citizens. Without robust IT infrastructure, e-governance initiatives would struggle to function effectively and provide the convenience, efficiency, and transparency that citizens expect in the digital age.Here are different components of IT infrastructure needed for successful e-government implementation:

  • Hardware Infrastructure: This includes servers, computers, networking devices, and storage systems necessary to support the e-government applications and services. It involves the setup and maintenance of data centers or cloud infrastructure to host and manage government systems and databases.
  • Network Infrastructure: A reliable and secure network infrastructure is crucial for egovernment. It includes network devices such as routers, switches, and firewalls, along with network connectivity, both internally within government offices and externally to connect with citizens, businesses, and other government entities. Network infrastructure enables data transmission, communication, and secure access to e-government systems.
  • Software and Applications: E-government relies on a wide range of software and applications tailored to specific government functions and services. This includes content management systems, customer relationship management systems, e-payment gateways, data analytics tools, and security software. The software infrastructure enables the development, deployment, and maintenance of e-government applications and services.
  • Data Management Systems: E-government involves the collection, storage, and management of vast amounts of data. A robust data management infrastructure includes databases, data warehouses, and data backup systems. It ensures secure storage, efficient retrieval, and data integrity. Data management systems also facilitate data analytics, enabling government entities to gain insights and make informed decisions based on the data.

Security Infrastructure: E-government requires a comprehensive security infrastructure to protect sensitive government data, systems, and citizen information. This includes firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, access controls, encryption mechanisms, and security protocols. Security infrastructure ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of e-government systems and prevents unauthorized access or data breaches.

questions.text: "E-Governance is to provide SMART government." Justify this statement .
questions.html: “E-Governance is to provide SMART government.” Justify this statement .
questions.answerHtml:
E-Governance, which focuses on using technology to improve government services, aligns with the idea of SMART government. SMART government means setting clear goals, using measurable ways to track progress, finding achievable and relevant solutions, and working within specific time frames. E-Governance aims to achieve these SMART goals by using technology to transform how governments work. It helps make government services more accessible, efficient, and transparent.

By adopting e-governance, governments can set specific targets like reducing paperwork and making services easier for citizens to access. They can measure progress using data and make sure their efforts are on track. E-governance also provides practical solutions that make sense in the digital age, like automating tasks and offering online platforms for citizens to interact with the government. Governments set deadlines to make sure changes happen quickly and meet people’s needs. Overall, e-governance supports the principles of SMART government by using technology to improve government operations and deliver services more effectively.

questions.text: What is E-Government maturity model? Describe the various maturity levels.
questions.html: What is E-Government maturity model? Describe the various maturity levels.
questions.answerHtml:
A maturity model is a method for judging the maturity of the processes of an organization and for identifying the key practices that are required to increase the maturity of these processes. An eGovernment maturity model provides us with guidance on how to gain control of our processes for developing and maintaining eGovernment services and how to evolve toward a culture of excellence in providing and managing eGovernment.

Closed

– Organizations are closed to e-governance. No plans or vision is available.

– They continue with fully manual and conventional operations.

– This is the stage when an organization does not use ICT as a facilitator for good governance and has no plans to do so in the near future.

– This situation may arise due to a lack of exposure to ICTs and associated benefits that again may depend upon a number of reasons: remoteness from the mainstream in terms of location is primary, and lack of resources and strategic thinking could be some of the other issues.

Initial

– The organization lacks strategic thinking and direction for e-governance at the top level.

– The effort sustains as long as the enthusiasm of the individual, who initiated it, remains and is often abandoned due to lack of direction.

– Such organizations generally accumulate hardware without any planning and much of it goes unutilized or underutilized.

– This level corresponds to the stage when an organization has initiated the automation of its processes but on an ad-hoc(On required) basis.

– No organized efforts are made to undertake the e-governance initiatives.

Planned

– E-governance is a part of the organization’s agenda.

– Strategic thinking and leadership guide the e-governance initiatives.

– Clear understanding of e-governance needs as projected by the external and internal customers/users.

– A need assessment study is conducted to prioritize areas of implementation and gauge the extent of e-readiness.

– Taking input from the assessment study, extensive planning has been carried out indicating policies, strategies, various activities, stakeholders, roles and responsibilities, and resources required in terms of time, money and manpower to undertake the e-governance exercise.

– However, the organization is yet to enter into the planned implementation of the e-governance exercise, even though all the requisite planning is completed.

Realized
– This level corresponds to the stage when the organization actually realizes the complete e-governance plan.

– Consequently, an integrated system is established where all the internal processes of the organization are computerized and there is seamless information exchange among all concerned entities.

– The organization starts delivering the services to its external as well as internal customers/users in an effective manner.

– Complete realization of the plan, in a single instance, would entail an enormous amount of resources in terms of time, money, and manpower, which may necessitate adopting a phased approach for the operation of the e-governance services.

Institutionalized
– At this level, the organizations sustain the realized state over a period of time so that e-governance becomes part of its work culture.

– The e-governance services are effectively utilized and accepted by the users.

– Several iterations between planned and realized states lead to institutionalization when e-governance becomes a way of life.

questions.text: How can we achieve good governance through E-Government models? Explain.
questions.html: How can we achieve good governance through E-Government models? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
We can achieve good governance through e-governance in the following ways:

  • Roles and responsibilities: There should be clarity regarding individual responsibilities, organizational expectations of executives, and the role of executive and steering committees.
  • Structure and composition: An executive committee needs to have the right group of people, having particular regard for each individual’s background, skills, and experience, and how the addition of individuals builds the collective capability and effective functioning of the committee.
  • Purpose and strategy: The executive committee plays an important role in setting the vision, purpose, and strategies of the organization, helping the organization understand these, and adapting the plans to implement them.
  • Risk management: By putting in place an appropriate system of risk oversight and internal controls, executive committees can help increase the likelihood that their organizations will deliver on their purpose.
  • Organizational performance: The executive committee determines and assesses appropriate performance categories and indicators for organization.
  • Committee effectiveness: An executive committee’s effectiveness may be greatly enhanced through careful planning of board-related activities; committee meetings being run efficiently; regular assessments of organizational performance; having an executive succession plan; and the effective use of sub-committees, where appropriate.
  • Accountability: The executive committee must ensure there is a flow of information to the board that aids decision-making; there is transparency and accountability to external. stakeholders and employees throughout the enterprise and the integrity of financial statements and other key information is safeguarded.
  • Organizational maturity: The executive committee has a role to play in enhancing the capacity and capabilities of the organization they serve.
  • Culture and ethics: The executive committee sets the tone for ethical and responsible decision-making throughout the organization.

questions.text: Define E-readiness. What is legal infrastructural preparedness?
questions.html: Define E-readiness. What is legal infrastructural preparedness?
questions.answerHtml:
E-Readiness is the ability to use information and communication technologies (ICT) to develop one’s economy and foster one’s welfare. It Is the ability to pursue value-creation opportunities facilitated by the use of the Internet. It is not simply a matter of the number of computer servers, websites, and mobile phones in the country, but also things such as its citizen’s ability to utilize technology skillfully, the transparency of its business and legal systems, and the extent to which governments encourage the use of digital technologies.

Legal infrastructural preparedness

  • The manual processes in government are usually obsolete, inefficient, and bureaucratic.
  • Though they have transformed to computerization practices, they continue to have poor and inefficient performance and this is due to a lack of administrative reforms and lack of business process reengineering.
  • They lack the requisite legislation and legal infrastructure to enable such reforms or reengineering of the existing business practices, rules, and regulations within the government at various levels.
  • This seems to be accentuated (emphasized) in developing countries while developed countries have been significantly successful in administrative reforms and business reengineering.
  • The fundamental question that arises here is “Are the laws and regulations required to permit and support the move towards e-governance initiatives in place? Example: Digital Signature Act

questions.text: What are the challenges to E-Governance security? Explain.
questions.html: What are the challenges to E-Governance security? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
1. Availability

It is the process of ensuring that information and vital IT services are available when required. Availability concerns affect publishing, interactive processing, transaction processing, and service delivery e-government activities. Following are some availability concerns:

  • Fault-related availability concerns: These include hardware faults, changes in program or data structures, and failures in other system facilities that are not computer-based.
  • Intrinsic availability concerns: These include unuse of storage and recovery mechanism, failure of magnetic media, and loss of facilities due to physical damage.
  • Denial of service concerns: Government services are attractive targets for malicious activities. Denial of service attacks can be launched from a variety of sources and can take a number of forms.
  • Individual or informally organized hackers: Most denials of-service attacks against e-government services have been launched by individual or informally organized hackers. Some of these have resulted in significant disruption and expense to the taxpayer.

2. Integrity:

It is the process of safeguarding the accuracy and completeness of information and software. Integrity concerns affect publishing, interactive processing, transaction processing, and service delivery e-government activities. Following are some integrity concerns:

  • Data Content Integrity issues: They are associated with unauthorized modification or destruction of e-government information content. This can involve the modification or destruction of information electronically published by the government or information associated with reports, applications, or other service requests.
  • Intentional modification of data: Data may be modified or destroyed within e-government processors (e.g. Web Servers). Penetration may be accomplished by defeating identification and authentication mechanisms.
  • Connection integrity issues: Successful implementation of e-government services requires some degree of confidence on the part of private citizens or other user entities that information being read originated only with the assumed government source and that information  being provided goes only to the appropriate government destination(s).

3. Confidentiality: 

It is the process of protecting sensitive information from unauthorized disclosure.

  • Impacts or consequences of unauthorized exposure: The consequences of unauthorized exposure of information via e-government resources depend in large part on the specific information that is exposed.
  • Loss of confidence in institutions and service delivery mechanisms: Public disclosure of e-government confidentiality breaches can result in loss of public confidence in e-government mechanisms and in the institutions they serve.

Impacts or consequences of unauthorized exposure: The consequences of unauthorized exposure of information via e-government resources depend in large part on the specific information that is exposed.

Loss of confidence in institutions and service delivery mechanisms: Public disclosure of e-government confidentiality breaches can result in loss of public confidence in e-government mechanisms and in the institutions they serve.

questions.text: Explain the uses of data warehousing and data mining in agriculture.
questions.html: Explain the uses of data warehousing and data mining in agriculture.
questions.answerHtml:
Data warehousing and data mining have significant applications in the field of agriculture. Here are some uses of data warehousing and data mining in agriculture:

  1. Crop Yield Analysis: Data warehousing and data mining can be utilized to store and analyze historical data related to crop yields, weather patterns, soil conditions, and farming practices. By analyzing this data, patterns, and correlations can be identified, enabling farmers and agricultural researchers to make informed decisions. Data mining techniques can help identify factors that contribute to high or low crop yields, leading to improved farming practices, optimized resource allocation, and increased agricultural productivity.
  2. Pest and Disease Management: Data warehousing and data mining can assist in monitoring and managing pests and diseases in agriculture. By analyzing historical data on pest and disease occurrences, climate conditions, and crop health, data mining techniques can help identify early warning signs and patterns. This enables farmers to implement pest and disease management strategies, such as timely interventions, precision spraying, and targeted use of pesticides.
  3. Market Analysis and Predictive Modeling: Data warehousing and data mining can be utilized to analyze market trends, consumer preferences, and price fluctuations in the agricultural sector. By analyzing historical market data and consumer behavior, predictive models can be developed to forecast demand, identify potential market opportunities, and optimize pricing and distribution strategies. This enables farmers and agricultural businesses to make data-driven decisions and adapt their production and marketing strategies to meet market demands effectively.

The security architecture of E-government is a high-level document that sets the security goals of the e-governance project and describes the procedure that needs to be followed by all the e-governance hierarchy such as businesses, and operations.

The appropriate legal framework is absolutely essential for the systematic and sustainable growth of e-government.

Land Reform is a program especially undertaken by a national government, involving the redistribution of agricultural land among the landless. It is the reform of the regulatory and administrative frameworks, including laws, regulations, and rules, for better management of land ownership. Nepal has been attempting to reform land relations for more than 50 years. Following are the issues facing equitable land ownership in Nepal today:

  • The real picture of land ownership is not known.
  • The rule of land law has been seriously undermined.
  • Divisions of positions and rising doubt.
  • Faith in the capacity of the state as a land reformer is low.

questions.text: Why do we need E-Governance? How can we use E-Governance to provide efficient services to citizens? Explain using suitable example.
questions.html: Why do we need E-Governance? How can we use E-Governance to provide efficient services to citizens? Explain using suitable example.
questions.answerHtml:
We need e-governance for the following reasons:

1. Increase efficiency and effectiveness of government works.

2. Smoother and faster delivery of govt works like distributing ID Cards, Citizenship certificates, and Issuing clearances to documents (land, Tax)

3. Direct accessibility for the citizens

4. Pro-active participation of Government representatives, Bureaucrats, and citizens

5. No Favouritism and Nepotism

6. Accountability

7. Increase Transparency

8. No Need to involve third parties by paying more money than required

9. Communication between citizens

10. To make govt officials respectful, responsible, and dutiful.

We use E-Govemance to provide efficient services to citizens. The eGovernment’s ultimate objective is to offer an enhanced portfolio of public services efficiently and cost-effectively to citizens. The e-government also could provide more transparency for the government, it enables the public to be informed about what the government is working on and the policies which are enforced. The primary benefit would replacing and optimizing the PaperBased System while implementing electronic government. That could save lots of time, money, and also the environment in return due to reducing paper consumption. The implementation of e-government could also promote better communication between government and business. For example, e-procurement as a subsidiary of e-government services could facilitate Communication between G2G and B2B that will allow smaller businesses to Compete with bigger companies in public tenders. Hence the benefit of e-government could be creating an open and transparent market and a stronger economy. Nowadays, companies and people can get information quicker and at any moment of the day in comparison to the past. E-government and its capacity could be available to all people regardless of their place or social level. In summary, more efficiency, enhanced services to better serve citizens, better accessibility of public services, and more transparency and accountability of government services are the expected advantages of e-government.

questions.text: What is E-Governance model? Explain broadcasting/wider dissemination model and critical flow model in detail.
questions.html: What is E-Governance model? Explain broadcasting/wider dissemination model and critical flow model in detail.
questions.answerHtml:
E-governance models are the frameworks of digital governance that are based on the inherent characteristics of ICT such as enabling equal access to information to anyone who is a part of the digital network and de-concentration of information across the entire sources of digital network, connecting all information. The information does not reside on any particular node but flows equally across all the nodes in the E-Governance Model.

Broadcasting/wider dissemination model

  • The broadcasting model is based on the mass dissemination of governance-related information which is already available in the public domain into the wider public domain using ICTs.
  • This raises awareness among the citizens about ongoing governance processes and government services that are available to them and how they can benefit from them.
  • The application of this model using appropriate technologies, could reduce the “information failure situations”.
  • The wider-dissemination model opens up an alternate channel for people to access information as well as validates information available in the local domain from external sources.

 

Applications

  1. Putting government laws and legislation online.
  2. Making available the names, contact addresses, emails, and fax no’s of local government officials online.
  3. Making available key information pertaining to governmental plans, and budgets.
  4. Putting key quote judgment/judicial statements that are of value to common citizens and creating our precedence for future actions online, viz. Key environment-related judgments, state v/s citizen court rulings, etc.

Merits:

  1. It enhances the ‘access’ and ‘flow’ of information to all segments of society.
  2. Government can use this model to provide greater governance services to their constituencies and to enhance the participation of citizens in governance processes.

Demerits:

  1. The model can lose its effectiveness
  2. In the situation of optimal ignorance
  3. In societies, where the free flow of information is not possible.

 

Critical flow model

  • The model is based on broadcasting information of ‘critical’ value (which by its very nature will not be disclosed by those involved with bad governance practices) to a targeted audience using ICTs and other tools. The targeted audience may include media, affected parties, opposition parties, the judicial bench, independent investigators, or the general public.
  • Those who would divulge(reveal) such information could include upright officials and workers, whistleblowers, affected parties, and those who were themselves involved in bad governance practices but have now changed their minds or may wish to trade such information for lenient(soft) punishments

Applications :

This model could be applied in the following possible ways :

  • Making available corruption-related data about a particular Ministry / Division/ Officials online to its electoral constituency or to the concerned regulatory body.
  • Making available Research studies, Enquiry reports, and Impact studies commissioned by the Government or Independent commissions to the affected parties.
  • Making Human Rights Violations cases violations freely available to Judiciary, NGOs, and concerned citizens.
  • Making available information that is usually suppressed, for instance, Environmental Information on radioactivity spills, effluents discharge, and information on green ratings of the company to the concerned community.

Merits :

  • This model is more directed and evolved.
  • Different organizations can use it differently depending on the aspect of governance and the situation they want to address.
  • The model corrects information failure, raises awareness about bad governance practices, and acts as a hindrance to bad governance practices.
  • Also, the model exerts indirect pressure on the concerned governance institution / policy-making body to move away from an optimal ignorance attitude to reform and take into cognizance the interest and opinion of the masses in decision-making processes.

Demerits :

  • The model may not work in cases where the governance mechanism does not allow public debates and opinions and censures all information of critical nature.

questions.text: Why do we need IT infrastructure to implement E-Governance? Explain network and computing infrastructure needed to implement E-governance.
questions.html: Why do we need IT infrastructure to implement E-Governance? Explain network and computing infrastructure needed to implement E-governance.
questions.answerHtml:
IT infrastructure is crucial for the implementation of e-governance because it forms the backbone of digital transformation and enables governments to deliver efficient and accessible services to citizens. It supports the development of digital platforms, websites, and applications through which citizens can access government information and interact with services.  Additionally, IT infrastructure facilitates the collection, storage, processing, and analysis of data, ensuring its security, privacy, and integrity. It also provides the necessary connectivity and communication channels for government entities to collaborate, share information, and engage with citizens. Without robust IT infrastructure, e-governance initiatives would struggle to function effectively and provide the convenience, efficiency, and transparency that citizens expect in the digital age.

Network Infrastructure for E-Commerce

The network infrastructure is the underlying foundation of the system. It forms the services that create the operating makeup of your network. In a Communications Services deployment, determining your network infrastructure from the project goals ensures that you will have an architecture that can scale and grow.

The Existing Network

We need to understand our existing network infrastructure to determine how well it can meet the needs of our deployment goals. We identify if we need to upgrade the existing network’s components or purchase new network components by examining our existing infrastructure. We should build up a complete map of the existing network by covering these areas:

  1. Physical communication links, such as cable length, grade, and so forth
  2. Communication links, such as analog, ISDN, VPN, T3, and so forth, and available bandwidth and latency between sites.
  3. server information, including Hostnames, IP addresses, Domain Name System (DNS) server for domain membership
  4. Locations of devices on your network, including Hubs, Switches, Modems, Routers and bridges, and Proxy servers.
  5. Number of users at each site, including mobile users

After completing this inventory, you need to review that information in conjunction with your project goals to determine what changes are required so that you can successfully deliver the deployment.

Network Infrastructure Components

Following common network infrastructure components have a direct impact on the success of your deployment: Routers and switches, Firewalls, Load balancers, Storage Area Networks (SAN), DNS,

Planning Your Network Infrastructure Layout

In deriving your infrastructure topology, you need to consider the following topics: Intranet, Internal network, Proxies, Firewall Configuration, Mobile users

Computing infrastructure

Computing Infrastructure provides management and support for end-user computers, servers, storage systems, operating systems, databases, middleware, and ERP systems. Three groups• make up the Computing Infrastructure team:

  • Database and ERP Administration
  • End-User Computing
  • Server & Storage Services

The Computing Infrastructure team has a vast collective set of skills and expertise in areas such as data center management, Storage Area Networks, desktop and server imaging, database administration, and general troubleshooting skills.

questions.text: Define E-Government. Explain E-Government as an Information System.
questions.html: Define E-Government. Explain E-Government as an Information System.
questions.answerHtml:
E-Government, also known as electronic government, refers to the use of information and communication technologies (ICT) to transform and improve the delivery of government services, processes, and interactions. It involves the digitalization of administrative procedures, the utilization of online platforms, and the integration of technology into governance practices. E-Government aims to enhance the efficiency, transparency, accessibility, and citizen-centricity of government operations, allowing citizens and businesses to interact with government entities electronically, access services online, and participate in decision-making processes.

E-Government can be viewed as an information system that leverages technology to facilitate the exchange, storage, processing, and management of information within a government context. It comprises various components that work together to support e-governance initiatives. These components include:

  • Hardware: The physical infrastructure such as computers, servers, networking devices, and mobile devices that enable data processing and communication.
  • Software: Applications, systems, and databases that support e-governance operations, including government portals, service platforms, data management systems, and security software.
  • Data: The information collected, stored, and processed within e-government systems, including citizen data, administrative records, policies, and public information.
  • Networks: The connectivity infrastructure that enables communication and data exchange between government entities, citizens, and businesses, including the internet, intranets, and secure communication channels.
  • People: The users and stakeholders involved in e-governance, including government officials, employees, citizens, businesses, and technology experts.

As an information system, e-government facilitates the digital transformation of government processes, automates administrative tasks, enables online service delivery, supports data-driven decision-making, and promotes citizen engagement.

questions.text: Why is it necessary to implement ICT in government? Explain.
questions.html: Why is it necessary to implement ICT in government? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
Implementing ICT (Information and Communication Technology) in government is necessary due to several compelling reasons. Firstly, it enhances efficiency by automating administrative processes and enabling streamlined data management. This reduces paperwork, bureaucratic delays, and manual errors, resulting in faster decision-making and improved operational efficiency within government agencies. ICT tools also facilitate collaboration, communication, and coordination among different government entities, enabling more effective and integrated governance.

ICT in government significantly improves service delivery to citizens. Digital platforms, online portals, and mobile applications allow citizens to access government information, submit applications, and receive services remotely and conveniently. This eliminates the need for physical visits, reduces waiting times, and enhances accessibility to government services. Additionally, ICT enables governments to provide personalized and citizen-centric services, addressing individual needs and preferences. This leads to greater satisfaction and a positive user experience.

ICT implementation promotes transparency, accountability, and citizen participation. Digital platforms and open data initiatives make government information and data more accessible to the public. Citizens can access information on government policies, decisions, and spending, fostering transparency and enabling public scrutiny. ICT also facilitates citizen engagement through mechanisms such as online feedback, participatory decision-making, and digital communication channels. This empowers citizens, enhances trust in government, and strengthens democratic processes.

e-governance plan.

all concerned entities.
– The organization starts delivering the services to its external as well as internal

– The e-governance services are effectively utilized and accepted by the users.
– Several iterations between planned and realized state lead to institutionalization, when
e-governance becomes a way of life.

questions.text: How can we achieve good governance through E-Government models? Explain.
questions.html: How can we achieve good governance through E-Government models? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
We can achieve good governance through e-governance in the following ways:

  • Roles and responsibilities: There should be clarity regarding individual responsibilities, organizational expectations of executives, and the role of executive and steering committees.
  • Structure and composition: An executive committee needs to have the right group of people, having particular regard for each individual’s background, skills, and experience, and how the addition of individuals builds the collective capability and effective functioning of the committee.
  • Purpose and strategy: The executive committee plays an important role in setting the vision, purpose, and strategies of the organization, helping the organization understand these, and adapting the plans to implement them.
  • Risk management: By putting in place an appropriate system of risk oversight and internal controls, executive committees can help increase the likelihood that their organizations will deliver on their purpose.
  • Organizational performance: The executive committee determines and assesses appropriate performance categories and indicators for organization.
  • Committee effectiveness: An executive committee’s effectiveness may be greatly enhanced through careful planning of board-related activities; committee meetings being run efficiently; regular assessments of organizational performance; having an executive succession plan; and the effective use of sub-committees, where appropriate.
  • Accountability: The executive committee must ensure there is a flow of information to the board that aids decision-making; there is transparency and accountability to external. stakeholders and employees throughout the enterprise and the integrity of financial statements and other key information is safeguarded.
  • Organizational maturity: The executive committee has a role to play in enhancing the capacity and capabilities of the organization they serve.
  • Culture and ethics: The executive committee sets the tone for ethical and responsible decision-making throughout the organization.

Roles and responsibilities: There should be clarity regarding individual responsibilities, organizational expectations of executives, and the role of executive and steering committees.

Structure and composition: An executive committee needs to have the right group of people, having particular regard for each individual’s background, skills, and experience, and how the addition of individuals builds the collective capability and effective functioning of the committee.

Purpose and strategy: The executive committee plays an important role in setting the vision, purpose, and strategies of the organization, helping the organization understand these, and adapting the plans to implement them.

questions.text: Define E-readiness. What is data system infrastructural preparedness and technological infrastructural preparedness?
questions.html: Define E-readiness. What is data system infrastructural preparedness and technological infrastructural preparedness?
questions.answerHtml:
E-Readiness is the ability to use information and communication technologies (ICT) to develop one’s economy and foster one’s welfare. It is the ability to pursue value-creation opportunities facilitated by the use of the Internet. It is a measure of the e-business environment, a collection of factors that indicate how amenable (willing) a market is to Internet-based opportunities.

Data System Infrastructural Preparedness

  • The core of e-governance is e-MIS which holds the entire database of any organization.
  • The data that were managed manually need to be computerized or brought into electronic form which means that the preparedness of a computerized database or data warehouse is required.
  • Data quality and data security are of prime concern here as most of the government infrastructures are not up to the mark in developing countries.
  • The major question that arises here is “Are all the requisite management information systems, records, databases, and work processes in the proper place so as to provide the quantity and quality of data to support the move to e-governance?”
  • This is the core computerization activity of a government process which may take several years to reach this stage.

Technological Infrastructural Preparedness

  • Technology is fast changing in the ICT domain and there is a rapid obsolescence of software as well as hardware which require great financial support time and again.
  • Government organizations encounter this situation especially as their procedures to procure hardware or software are very inefficient and slow.
  • The technological infrastructure in developing countries including computing and telecommunication is absent. As a result software and hardware may not be compatible. The major reasons are the cost of technology, Adaptability, and Obsolescence (undesirable) . This is a serious limitation of e-governance implementation.

questions.text: What are different approaches to E-Governance security? Explain.
questions.html: What are different approaches to E-Governance security? Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
Security is one of the most important issues in E-governance. All of the security approaches that are common in E-commerce are applicable to E-governance. But E-governance is a little different from E-commerce. Usually, government networks can communicate to each other better than business networks, because, most of them are connected for transferring information, but businesses are competitors and they don’t disclose their sensitive information, so the security of E-government is much more important as compared to E-commerce. Today the users or programmers (Hackers or abusers!) are very smart and intelligent, and they can attack in several forms and so the defense level has to be sufficiently strong and comprehensive.

Some approaches to E-governance security are:

  • Security at the User Level

Security at the user level is a very important issue. We can classify user-level security management into three parts:

  1. Identity Management– The main purpose of this is to create a unique digital identity or credential for all legal users by providing a unique username and password, to create and manage ICT systems that ensure that the digital identities are secure.
  2. Access Management System– In this level, the unique credentials which are provided to the user at the identity level are matched to identify the user, that he/she is actually an authentic person.
  3. Interaction Management System– Interaction management is a most comprehensive and complex phase. It includes assurance of the Integrity, Confidentiality, and Non-repudiation principles of comprehensive security.

At the user level, we can use various tools such as digital identity tokens, public key infrastructure (PKI), digital signatures, asymmetric key cryptography, etc. to provide or enhance security at the user level.

 

  • Security at the Transport Level

At this level, we consider e-governance security in two aspects which are security within LAN and WAN, and the second one is Security over the Internet. This security level is classified into two systems, i.e. Secure Communication System and Cryptographic System.

The data and information reach through user to ICT assets or vice-versa, and when the data is in between these two i.e. in transmission medium which can be either LAN, WAN, or any wireless or any other medium, then we need higher security. For this e-governance, administrators use various tools or techniques like creating a Virtual Private Network (VPN), installing Firewalls, Antiviruses, and using higher and more complex Encryption or decryption techniques, etc.

questions.text: Explain the uses of data warehousing and data mining in health, education and the rural development.
questions.html: Explain the uses of data warehousing and data mining in health, education and the rural development.
questions.answerHtml:
The data warehouse is an integrated collection of data extracted from operational, historical, and external databases that have been cleaned, transformed, and cataloged for retrieval and analysis to provide business intelligence for business decision-making.

Rural Development: 

  • By analyzing data related to infrastructure needs, population demographics, and economic indicators, data warehousing and data mining can inform decisions regarding the allocation of resources for rural development projects. This enables governments and organizations to plan and implement infrastructure projects that address the specific needs of rural communities. Data on individuals below the poverty line can be built into a data warehouse.
  • Drinking water census data (from the drinking water mission) can be effectively utilized by OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) and data mining technologies.
  • Monitoring and analysis of progress made on the implementation of rural development programs can also be made using OLAP and data mining technologies.

Health:

  • Data warehousing and data mining can be used to store and analyze vast amounts of health-related data, such as patient records, clinical trials, and medical literature. Researchers can leverage this data to identify patterns, correlations, and insights that contribute to medical research, drug development, and treatment advancements.
  • Community needs assessment data, immunization data, and data from national programs on controlling blindness, leprosy, and malaria can all be used for data warehousing implementation, OLAP, and data mining applications.

Education:

  • Data warehousing and data mining can be used to collect and analyze data on student performance, attendance, and behavior. This enables educators to identify patterns, trends, and factors that influence student success. The insights gained can inform interventions, personalized learning strategies, and targeted support programs to improve educational outcomes.
  • Data warehousing and data mining support learning analytics, which involves analyzing student data and interactions within learning management systems, online platforms, and educational applications. This data helps educators understand student engagement, learning patterns, and areas where students may need additional support or intervention.

questions.text: How can we use human resource management software to support E-Government?  Explain.
questions.html: How can we use human resource management software to support E-Government?  Explain.
questions.answerHtml:
Human resource management (HRM) software can play a vital role in supporting e-government initiatives by streamlining and optimizing human resource processes and functions. Here’s how HRM software can contribute to e-government:

  1. Efficient Workforce Management: HRM software enables efficient management of government employees, including recruitment, onboarding, performance management, and training. It automates administrative tasks such as employee data management, leave and attendance tracking, and performance evaluations. This streamlines HR processes, reduces paperwork, and increases efficiency in managing the government workforce.
  2. Enhanced Employee Self-Service: HRM software often includes employee self-service portals or mobile These platforms allow government employees to access their personal information, update their profiles, apply for leave, view payslips, and access relevant HR policies and documents. By providing self-service capabilities, HRM software reduces the administrative burden on HR departments, empowers employees with direct access to information, and enhances overall employee experience and satisfaction.
  3. Data Integration and Analytics: HRM software can integrate with other e-government systems, such as payroll, finance, and performance management systems, to ensure seamless data flow and consistency. This integration enables the generation of comprehensive reports and analytics on workforce demographics, performance metrics, training needs, and employee satisfaction.

By leveraging HRM software as part of e-government initiatives, government entities can streamline HR processes, improve workforce management, and enhance employee experiences. The automation of administrative tasks, employee self-service capabilities, and data-driven insights contribute to efficient HR operations and effective utilization of human resources. This ultimately supports the goals of e-governance by promoting transparency, efficiency, and citizen-centric service delivery.

questions.text: Write short notes on:  a. Electronic service delivery  b. IT in judiciary
questions.html:
Write short notes on:

a. Electronic service delivery

b. IT in judiciary
questions.answerHtml:
Electronic service delivery: Electronic service delivery (ESD) in e-governance refers to the provision of government services to citizens and businesses through digital channels, such as online platforms, mobile applications, and electronic means. Through online platforms and mobile applications, individuals can access government services anytime and from anywhere with internet connectivity. This eliminates the need for physical visits to government offices, reduces waiting times, and expands service availability to remote areas. ESD can lead to cost savings for both citizens and government entities. Citizens save on transportation costs and avoid time off from work for physical visits to government offices. From the government’s perspective, ESD reduces the need for physical infrastructure, paperwork, and manual processing, resulting in operational cost savings. Some examples of ESD are Online Tax Filing, Online Payments, Billing, etc.

IT in Judiciary: 

Information Technology (IT) plays a crucial role in the judiciary, transforming the way courts and legal systems operate. An example of IT in the Judiciary is a case management system. IT enables the implementation of electronic case management systems, which digitally store and manage case-related information, documents, and records. These systems streamline court processes, facilitate efficient scheduling and tracking of cases, and enable judges, lawyers, and other stakeholders to access case information electronically. Case management systems improve the efficiency of court operations, reduce paperwork, and enhance transparency and accountability.

questions.text: Differentiate between e-Government and e-Governance. What are the various stages of E-governance?
questions.html: Differentiate between e-Government and e-Governance. What are the various stages of E-governance?
questions.answerHtml:
E-governance E-government
It is the use of information and communication technologies (ICT) to transform traditional governance by making it accessible, transparent, effective, and accountable. It is the government that is already using ICT serves to improve government activities and process.
It focuses on citizens and their interaction with the government. It focuses on government operations and service delivery.
Its outcome is: Empowering citizens and promoting democracy. Its outcome is: Efficiency, cost saving, better service delivery.
Examples: Online voting, citizen feedback mechanisms, etc. Examples: Digital record keeping, online tax filing, etc.
The decisions of E-governance involve multiple stakeholders. Decisions are primarily made by the government.
Challenges: Citizen adoption, digital divide, privacy Challenges: Interoperability, legacy systems.
E-governance generally never comes alone, it includes E-government. E-government is a part of E-governance.
E-governance is functional. E-government is a system only.
It is a two-way protocol. It is a one-way protocol.

 

The various stages of e-governance are:

Stage – 1 (Presence): The presence of information on the various platforms of government such as websites, e-brochures etc makes the first stage of E-governance. In the first stage, the activity involves the development and establishment and delivery of information for stakeholder use. This stage is the simplest, non-expensive phase in the implementation of E-governance, but it gives only little option for the stakeholders. For example, the website of the Ministry of environment publishes only cursory information about the ministry, information of officers, their contact details, address for communication, report they published, various orders etc, but there is a one-way flow of information and don’t have interactive capabilities.

Stage – 2 (Interaction): The second stage of the E-governance model is the advanced version of the first stage which involves the interaction between the government and stakeholders such as businessmen or interested groups or citizens. It is a two-way communication or interaction which involves the real means of communication. In this stage citizens or stakeholders can communicate with the government via E-mail, chat database, customer care platform, feedback forms or submission of online forms. It ensures the transparency of communication and accountability of government offices. It also reduces the physical interaction of stakeholders and governance, which also saves labour hours.

Stage – 3 (Transaction): The third stage of E-governance involves the transactions made between
stakeholder and government. In this stage, the government’s e-governance efforts make the life of citizens easier by enabling electronic transactions and simplifying government processes. Government, Businesses and Departments can avail services by making a payment online for services such as licence renewal, online bidding and deposition of the bid amount, paying taxes online, and paying for various services provided by the government. The level of interaction in this stage is higher than in the second stage and more activities are involved in the flow of information, mainly one-way activities such as government to client or client to government. Eg. Bidding for procurement, licence renewal fee payment, fee payment for a patent application, submission of job application with fee payment etc.

Stage– 4 (Transformation): This phase is the highest in order for e-governance initiatives. This level
involves exhausting the full use of available technology to transform the government service by receiving information, organisation and analysing information and execution. This is the two-way flow of information to improve the stakeholder relationship with the government and the service provider
should have robust capabilities to handle the issues, needs, and solving of problems of stakeholders. Right now there are very few options in the government that follow this phase of E-governance. The
main advantage of this stage is to provide a seamless flow of information by the service provider and collaborative decision-making among the union, state, local, citizens and private interest groups. It
removes the organisational barrier as well as reduces the Red-tapism behaviour of government officers by sticking them to follow time-bound decision-making. Eg. E-court, Virtual summit etc.

questions.text: Explain with example of maturity model of e-governance.
questions.html: Explain with example of maturity model of e-governance.
questions.answerHtml:
A maturity model is a method for judging the maturity of the processes of an organization and for identifying the key practices that are required to increase the maturity of these processes. An eGovernment maturity model provides us with guidance on how to gain control of our processes for developing and maintaining eGovernment services and how to evolve toward a culture of excellence in providing and managing eGovernment.

Closed

– Organizations are closed to e-governance. No plans or vision is available.

– They continue with fully manual and conventional operations.

– This is the stage when an organization does not use ICT as a facilitator for good governance and has no plans to do so in the near future.

– This situation may arise due to a lack of exposure to ICTs and associated benefits that again may depend upon a number of reasons: remoteness from the mainstream in terms of location is primary, and lack of resources and strategic thinking could be some of the other issues.

Initial

– The organization lacks strategic thinking and direction for e-governance at the top level.

– The effort sustains as long as the enthusiasm of the individual, who initiated it, remains and is often abandoned due to lack of direction.

– Such organizations generally accumulate hardware without any planning and much of it goes unutilized or underutilized.

– This level corresponds to the stage when an organization has initiated the automation of its processes but on an ad-hoc(On required) basis.

– No organized efforts are made to undertake the e-governance initiatives.

Planned

– E-governance is a part of the organization’s agenda.

– Strategic thinking and leadership guide the e-governance initiatives.

– Clear understanding of e-governance needs as projected by the external and internal customers/users.

– A need assessment study is conducted to prioritize areas of implementation and gauge the extent of e-readiness.

– Taking input from the assessment study, extensive planning has been carried out indicating policies, strategies, various activities, stakeholders, roles and responsibilities, and resources required in terms of time, money and manpower to undertake the e-governance exercise.

– However, the organization is yet to enter into the planned implementation of the e-governance exercise, even though all the requisite planning is completed.

Realized
– This level corresponds to the stage when the organization actually realizes the complete e-governance plan.

– Consequently, an integrated system is established where all the internal processes of the organization are computerized and there is seamless information exchange among all concerned entities.

– The organization starts delivering the services to its external as well as internal customers/users in an effective manner.

– Complete realization of the plan, in a single instance, would entail an enormous amount of resources in terms of time, money, and manpower, which may necessitate adopting a phased approach for the operation of the e-governance services.

Institutionalized
– At this level, the organizations sustain the realized state over a period of time so that e-governance becomes part of its work culture.

– The e-governance services are effectively utilized and accepted by the users.

– Several iterations between planned and realized states lead to institutionalization when e-governance becomes a way of life.

– This level corresponds to the stage when the organization actually realizes the complete e-governance plan.

– Consequently, an integrated system is established where all the internal processes of the organization are computerized and there is seamless information exchange among all concerned entities.

– The organization starts delivering the services to its external as well as internal customers/users in an effective manner.

– Complete realization of the plan, in a single instance, would entail an enormous amount of resources in terms of time, money, and manpower, which may necessitate adopting a phased approach for the operation of the e-governance services.

Institutionalized

– At this level, the organizations sustain the realized state over a period of time so that e-governance becomes part of its work culture.

– The e-governance services are effectively utilized and accepted by the users.

– Several iterations between planned and realized states lead to institutionalization when e-governance becomes a way of life.

questions.text: Explain the components of data warehouse. What are the applications of data mining in eGovernance in the context of Nepal.
questions.html: Explain the components of data warehouse. What are the applications of data mining in eGovernance in the context of Nepal.
questions.answerHtml:
The Components of a Data Warehouse are:

1. Data Sources: These are the various databases, applications, and systems from which data is extracted and loaded into the data warehouse. Data sources can include operational databases, spreadsheets, CRM systems, ERP systems, and more.

2. Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading (ETL): ETL is the process of extracting data from different sources, transforming it into a consistent format, and loading it into the data warehouse. This step ensures that data is clean, integrated, and ready for analysis.

3. Data Storage: The data warehouse stores data in a structured manner to enable efficient querying and analysis. Common storage methods include star schema, snowflake schema, and data cubes.

4. Data Modeling: Data modeling involves creating a logical representation of the data in the data warehouse, such as dimensional models, to facilitate efficient querying and reporting.

5. Metadata: Metadata contains information about the data in the data warehouse, including data definitions, data sources, transformation rules, and relationships between data elements.

6. Query and Reporting Tools: These tools allow users to access and query the data warehouse to generate reports, perform ad-hoc analysis, and gain insights from the data.

7. Data Governance: Data governance encompasses policies, procedures, and rules to ensure data quality, security, and compliance within the data warehouse.

 

Applications of Data Mining in e-Governance in the Context of Nepal:
– Data mining can help identify fraudulent activities and transactions in various government processes, such as tax collection, public procurement, and social welfare programs.

– Data mining can assist in optimizing resource allocation by analyzing historical data and patterns to identify areas where resources are most needed and where they can be best utilized.

– By analyzing data from various government departments and agencies, data mining can aid in policy formulation, decision-making processes, and evidence-based governance.

– Data mining can be used to analyze citizen behavior, preferences, and feedback, which can help in improving public services and tailoring governance initiatives to meet citizens’ needs.

– Data mining can be applied to predict demand for public services, such as healthcare, education, and transportation, allowing government agencies to better plan and allocate resources accordingly.

questions.text: Explain the critical flow model in e-Governance.
questions.html: Explain the critical flow model in e-Governance.
questions.answerHtml:
Critical flow model

– The model is based on broadcasting information of ‘critical’ value (which by its very nature will not be disclosed by those involved with bad governance practices) to a targeted audience using ICTs and other tools. The targeted audience may include media, affected parties, opposition parties, judicial bench, independent investigators, or the general public.

– Those who would divulge(reveal) such information could include upright officials and workers, whistleblowers, affected parties, and those who were themselves involved in bad governance practices but have now changed their minds or may wish to trade such information for lenient(soft) punishments

Applications :

This model could be applied in the following possible ways :

– Making available corruption-related data about a particular Ministry / Division/ Officials online to its electoral constituency or to the concerned regulatory body.

– Making available Research studies, Enquiry reports, and Impact studies commissioned by the Government or Independent commissions to the affected parties.

– Making Human Rights Violations cases violations freely available to Judiciary, NGOs, and concerned citizens.

– Making available information that is usually suppressed, for instance, Environmental Information on radioactivity spills, effluents discharge, and Information on green ratings of the company to the concerned community.

Merits :

– This model is more directed and evolved.

– Different organizations can use it differently depending on the aspect of governance and the situation they want to address.

– The model corrects information failure, raises awareness about bad governance practices, and acts as a hindrance to bad governance practices.

– Also, the model exerts indirect pressure on the concerned governance institution / policy-making body to move away from an optimal ignorance attitude to reform and take into cognizance the interest and opinion of the masses in decision-making processes.

Demerits :
– The model may not work in cases where the governance mechanism does not allow public debates and opinions and censures all information of critical nature.

questions.text: What do you mean by e-Readiness framework? Explain with example.
questions.html: What do you mean by e-Readiness framework? Explain with example.
questions.answerHtml:
E-Readiness is the ability to use information and communication technologies (ICT) to develop one’s economy and foster one’s welfare. It Is the ability to pursue value-creation opportunities facilitated by the use of the Internet. It is not simply a matter of the number of computer servers, websites, and mobile phones in the country, but also things such as its citizen’s ability to utilize technology skillfully, the transparency of its business and legal systems, and the extent to which governments encourage the use of digital technologies.
Example: Legal infrastructural preparedness

Legal infrastructural preparedness

– The manual processes in government are usually obsolete, inefficient, and bureaucratic.

– Though they have transformed to computerization practices, they continue to have poor and inefficient performance and this is due to a lack of administrative reforms and a lack of business process reengineering.

– They lack the requisite legislation and legal infrastructure to enable such reforms or reengineering of the existing business practices, rules, and regulations within the government at various levels.

– This seems to be accentuated (emphasized) in developing countries while developed countries have been significantly successful in administrative reforms and business reengineering.

– The fundamental question that arises here is “Are the laws and regulations required to permit and support the move towards e-governance initiatives in place?

– E.g Digital Signature Act

questions.text: Discuss the main impact of e-Governance application in digital divide.
questions.html: Discuss the main impact of e-Governance application in digital divide.
questions.answerHtml:
e-Governance applications can have both positive and negative impacts on the digital divide, which refers to the gap between those who have access to and can effectively use information and communication technologies (ICTs) and those who do not. Its main impacts:

1. Bridging the Divide:

e-Governance applications have the potential to bridge the digital divide by providing greater access to government services and information. As e-Governance initiatives are implemented, citizens can access public services, interact with government agencies, and obtain information online. This can be especially beneficial for people in remote or underserved areas who may have limited access to physical government offices.

2. Empowerment and Participation:

e-Governance applications can empower citizens to participate more actively in the governance process. e-Governance initiatives are accessible to all citizens, regardless of their digital literacy or access to technology.

3. Digital Literacy and Skills Gap:
The success of e-Governance applications depends on the digital literacy and skills of the citizens. People who lack digital literacy or skills may find it challenging to navigate e-Governance platforms and understand the processes involved. Governments need to invest in digital literacy programs and support to ensure that citizens can effectively use these services.

4. Privacy and Security Concerns:
e-Governance applications deal with sensitive citizen data, and security and privacy are critical concerns. A digital divide can be exacerbated if some citizens are apprehensive about using e-Governance services due to concerns about data breaches or misuse of personal information.

questions.text: What are the current trends of e-Governance development in Nepal.
questions.html: What are the current trends of e-Governance development in Nepal.
questions.answerHtml: Although Nepal stands at the lower position in the global scenario of ICT, there have been noticeable developments in the ICT sector in recent years. The telecommunication facilities have improved remarkably. The academic institutions/universities producing ICT professional resources have been expanded. Communication technologies, both electronic and print media, have extended their access to general people. Uses of the Internet, emails. and computers are gaining popularity. Several e-government applications are being introduced. Among the country’s recent e-government initiatives. Nepal’s e-government Master Plan was completed in November 2006. Another milestone is the preparation of an ICT Development Project which has worked out detailed investment proposals for prioritized projects. The Government of Nepal is thus keen and committed to promoting e-government for the implementation of various G2G, G2C, and G2B projects defined under respective priority areas.

questions.text: Explain the Comparative Analysis Model with example.
questions.html: Explain the Comparative Analysis Model with example.
questions.answerHtml:
Comparative Analysis Model
• The Comparative Analysis Model is based on exploring the information available in the public or private domain and comparing it with the actual known information sets to derive strategic learnings and arguments.

• This model empowers people by comparing cases of bad governance with those of good governance and identifying specific aspects of bad governance, the reasons and people behind them, and how the situation can be improved.

• The comparison could be made over a time scale to get a snapshot of the past and the present situation or could be used to compare the effectiveness of an intervention by comparing two similar situations.

Applications:

• To learn from past policies and actions and derive learning lessons for future policy-making.

• To evaluate the effectiveness of the current policies and identify key learning in terms of strengths and flaws in the policies.

• To effectively establish conditions of precedence, especially in the case of Judicial or legal decision-making ( for resolving (patent-related disputes, public goods ownership rights), and use it to influence/ advocate future decision-making.

• To evaluate the performance and track record of a particular decision-maker/decision-making body.

Merits :

• Based on the existing sets of information

• Watch-guard organizations and monitor groups can use this model to continuously track the governance past record and performance and compare with different information sets.

Demerits :

• Requires the ability to analyze and bring out strong arguments

• Ineffective in the absence of a strong civil society interest and public memory which is essential to force decision-makers to improve existing governance practices.
